The project's records do not show all of this as met, so it may not hold in full: REQ-1471 The server holds a viewer's connection event for the first SELECT and sends the program one connected event (to be rechecked on livedevelopment); REQ-1472 A connection's selection comes only from SELECT, and the server forwards only the selected sub-page (to be rechecked on livedevelopment); REQ-1474 The server keeps no channel content beyond per-connection state, one last-sent sub-page per connection, and a short cache of public pages' descriptions (to be rechecked on livedevelopment); REQ-1481 A selection the program does not answer in time ends with DENIED 503 and the connection stays open (to be rechecked on livedevelopment); REQ-1502 Each live connection has exactly one selection, made of one page number and one sub-code (to be rechecked on main); REQ-6719 The viewer-state exchange happens at the start of every push connection: a challenge after WELCOME, answered before SELECT, and connected held for the answer (not implemented on main); REQ-6881 A snapshot connection is answered with the page its program draws for a stranger, or its public description, and closed: no viewer, no challenge, no connection told, no session (to be rechecked on livedevelopment).

WhenWhat the connection is sent
At connectionWELCOME, then at once STATE_CHALLENGE, before any page, which the receiver answers with STATE_PROOF or STATE_NONE before it sends SELECT (viewer state's exchange). Nothing more until the program answers connected, which the server holds until the receiver has answered the challenge, or 10,000 ms have passed (the connection then has no viewer), and for the first SELECT. Then the channel's index records, the one sub-page the selection shows, its LINKS record when it has links, and its page's SUBPAGES records when the program sends a list.
The selection changes, by SELECT or the program's page redirectThe one sub-page the new selection shows, whole, with its LINKS record, and, if the connection lacks the list's current version, its page's SUBPAGES records
The program sends a new version of the selected sub-pageThat sub-page as changed rows, followed by its LINKS record when it has links
The program sends any other sub-pageNothing: a sub-page reaches a connection only when it is that connection's selection
The program changes the selected page's sub-page listThe new SUBPAGES records
The program ends the selection with deniedDENIED with its status, at once
The program does not answer within 5,000 ms, or is not runningDENIED 503
No SELECT within FIRST_SELECTION_WAIT_MS of connecting, or a receiver with no SELECT capabilityThe sub-page the program's reply gives for the channel's initial page, which is then the connection's selection, and no other
A SELECT repeats a selection DENIED endedAs a new selection, with a new number and a new deadline
A message of input units is read, with a selection madeThe next page frame ends with a cursor record that carries the acknowledgement. With no frame within 250 ms of the first input it covers, a cursor record goes alone.

This table is a viewer's connection's. A snapshot connection, one whose WELCOME agreed SNAPSHOT, is sent only what that item says: no STATE_CHALLENGE, no index, and its program is never told connected.

The program is the only source of content: the server answers nothing from a store, and keeps no page, sub-page, index or version between connections or across a restart.

A connection's sub-page never changes by itself. A program that sends another sub-page of the selected page does not change what is shown: it is not forwarded.

Not built. How a selected sub-page's object pages reach a receiver now that a program is the only source is not designed.

Rests on: EN 300 706 V1.2.1 clause 9.6.1 Packets X/27/0 to X/27/3 for Editorial Linking; EN 300 706 V1.2.1 clause A.1 Page numbering

5.4 A snapshot connection

DOC-6888 · reference · normative · NeoTeletext's own: no standard defines it · requirements REQ-6879, REQ-6880, REQ-6881, REQ-6882

Unfinished. The project's records do not show all of this as met, so it may not hold in full: REQ-6879 The push protocol's capability bit 25, SNAPSHOT, and the snapshot request a receiver sends: HELLO then one SELECT, closed at once when WELCOME does not agree it (tested, not recorded as met on livedevelopment); REQ-6880 The web agent's snapshot mode fetches one page as a stranger: the descriptor, then one snapshot connection or one page file, with nothing that identifies the viewer (tested, not recorded as met on livedevelopment); REQ-6881 A snapshot connection is answered with the page its program draws for a stranger, or its public description, and closed: no viewer, no challenge, no connection told, no session (to be rechecked on livedevelopment); REQ-6882 Snapshot connections and the program's snapshot drawing are limited by named constants per address, per channel and per program, apart from the viewer limits, with a cache of answers (tested, not recorded as met on livedevelopment).

A snapshot connection asks a live channel for one page as a stranger sees it, and nothing else. A receiver uses one to show a picture of a page it has not looked at, such as a browser's picture of a tab after a restart. It carries nothing that identifies the viewer, and the channel creates no viewer for it.

The receiver. It opens the push connection with no viewer key, cookie or session, and sends one message: HELLO with caps of exactly SNAPSHOT, SELECT, and REGIS and NAPLPS when it draws them, with no AGENT, then SELECT of one display page, with a sub-code or without one for the page as a whole, and no query. It sends nothing else, ever. When WELCOME does not agree SNAPSHOT it closes the connection at once with code 1000, before anything else: a server that does not know the bit treats the connection as a viewer's, and closing before any answer creates no viewer there and tells its program nothing. A STATE_CHALLENGE on a snapshot connection is a protocol error. It does not reconnect.

The channel. It agrees SNAPSHOT only when offered, with SELECT and the picture languages offered, never CURSOR, TOUCH or RESUME; a HELLO that offers SNAPSHOT without SELECT is a protocol error. It sends no STATE_CHALLENGE, creates and counts no viewer, and tells its program of no connection: it may ask its program to draw the page for no one in particular (snapshots, for a program), in a request that names no connection and no viewer. Anything after HELLO but one SELECT of a display page is a protocol error. It answers:

WhenWhat the connection is sent, then a close with code 1000
The program draws the page for a stranger, or the page is public and its description's sub-page is the one selected or the page was selected as a wholeThat sub-page, whole, as a selection's first sub-page is sent, with no index, LINKS, SUBPAGES, cursor, rule table, sound or animation record; then, when it has a picture in a language the connection agreed, its REGIS or NAPLPS record, with a NAPLPS picture's objects as one NAPLPS_OBJECTS record as they stand, and no DRAWING_LINKS or REGIS_CURSOR; in a language not agreed, the picture as Level 1 mosaics on the sub-page
The program declines or does not answer, and the page is reserved, not public, not described within 2,000 ms, or its description's sub-page is not the one selectedDENIED 404
The program could not be asked because of its snapshot rate, and the description does not answerDENIED 429
No program is runningDENIED 503
A limit on snapshot connections is reachedWELCOME agreeing SNAPSHOT, then DENIED 429 with no place
10,000 ms since the connection openedDENIED 503 if a SELECT stands unanswered

A channel MAY answer a snapshot connection with the same page for up to a minute after it was drawn: a snapshot is the page as anyone arriving would see it.

The NeoTeletext server's limits, per channel: 120 snapshot connections a minute from one network address, 8 open at once from one address, 1,024 open at once in all, apart from the limits on viewers; a snapshot never counts as a new viewer. It asks its program to draw at most 10 snapshots a second, with a burst of 20, at most 16 at once, each place at most once a minute, and waits 2,000 ms for each; snapshots share the description rate with web visitors. All are provisional until measured.

SNAPSHOT is bit 25 of the capabilities and raises no version: see Capabilities.

5.5 The records

DOC-1951 · reference · normative · NeoTeletext's own: no standard defines it · requirements REQ-36, REQ-1462, REQ-1480, REQ-6336, REQ-6528, REQ-6529, REQ-6761

Unfinished. The project's records do not show all of this as met, so it may not hold in full: REQ-36 Record framing (to be rechecked on livedevelopment); REQ-1462 Server sends only valid packets downstream (to be rechecked on main); REQ-1480 Every program message that reaches a viewer is sent as checked T42 packets (to be rechecked on livedevelopment); REQ-6529 The engine MUST time everything shown in 60 ticks a second and carry animation: FRAME, ANIMATE, SPRITES, NAPLPS_OBJECTS and SHEET records, teletext sprites, damage repaint (to be rechecked on livedevelopment); REQ-6761 Capability bits REGIS_CAP (23) and NAPLPS_CAP (24, NAPLPS on the raster from line 20), and DRAWING_LINKS and REGIS_CURSOR naming NAPLPS objects too (PAR-1, PAR-2, RAS-9) (to be rechecked on livedevelopment).

Everything a channel says beyond its pages is a record of the record frame, carried on data channel 12 in packets 4/31, which a decoder that knows none of them skips. A record has a type of its own in the frame, so a receiver that reads only some types skips the others by the type byte alone, before reading any field.

TypeRecordFragmentsHolds
1, 2, 3OBJECT, DATA, CONTROLAnySound
4CursorOneWhere the cursor is, and what has been acknowledged
5ControlOneWELCOME
6IndexOne or moreThe channel's magazines and pages
7LOGOne or moreA log line for the channel's author
8NoneNoneRetired. It was SET_COOKIE, withdrawn with cookies: no server sends it, and a receiver skips it as a type it does not read
9LINKSOne or moreA sub-page's Link Extension links
10SUBPAGESOne or moreA page's list of sub-pages
11REDIRECTOne or moreMoves a connection's viewer
12DENIEDOneA selection refused
14REGISOne or moreBytes of a sub-page's ReGIS picture
15DRAWING_LINKSOne or moreThe drawings of a sub-page's ReGIS picture, or the objects of its NAPLPS picture, that are links
16REGIS_CURSOROneThe drawing or object that is a sub-page's picture's cursor
17NAPLPSOne or moreBytes of a sub-page's NAPLPS picture
21RULESOne or moreA page's rule table, or that it has none
22RULES_QUERYOneA question, asked once, for a page's local state
23ANIMATEOne or moreOperations on the animation state of a sub-page's objects
24SPRITESOne or moreA teletext sub-page's sprites
25NAPLPS_OBJECTSOne or moreA NAPLPS sub-page's objects
26SHEETOne or moreBytes of a page's sprite sheet
27FRAMEOneThe beginning or the end of an atomic frame
28 to 33LOCAL_MIDI, VARIABLE, TIMER, REPORT, RUN, SEQUENCEOneA rule table's commands, sent directly by the server for a page and sub-code

The NeoTeletext server sends its records on audio service 0, and the record id starts at 0 with WELCOME and counts on from one record to the next on a connection, whatever its type, modulo 256. A value may be skipped, so a receiver uses the id only to gather a record's fragments. An encoder checks what it writes with its reader, so that a server cannot send what a receiver refuses.

Each record's layout is defined once, in its own item, and the reasons each has a type of its own are that the control record is one fragment, 26 bytes of body, and the others need more.

5.6 Records of several fragments, and records a receiver cannot use

DOC-1952 · reference · normative · NeoTeletext's own: no standard defines it · requirements REQ-40, REQ-494, REQ-1462

Unfinished. The project's records do not show all of this as met, so it may not hold in full: REQ-40 Broadcast carriage (to be rechecked on livedevelopment); REQ-494 Server push over the channel's WebSocket (to be rechecked on livedevelopment); REQ-1462 Server sends only valid packets downstream (to be rechecked on main).

Fragments. A record of more than 34 bytes is cut into fragments of 34 bytes, the last padded with zeros, at most 241 fragments, a record of at most 8,192 bytes. Each fragment is one packet with the record id, its index and the CRC-16. A channel sends a record's fragments in order, fragment 0 first, in one binary message or in consecutive ones. A receiver reassembles them by record id, and knows the record's length, and so its fragments, from fragment 0's frame header.

A record a receiver cannot use, a frame whose CRC-32, version or length fails, a field outside its range, text that breaks its rule, or bytes after the last field, is discarded whole and nothing of it applied. Each of its packets is counted as an invalid packet, and the connection is not closed. A LINKS record refused leaves its sub-page shown with no Link Extension links.

A record of a type a receiver does not read is skipped, and not counted.

5.7 The control record: WELCOME

DOC-1953 · reference · normative · NeoTeletext's own: no standard defines it · requirements REQ-205, REQ-210, REQ-6927

Unfinished. The project's records do not show all of this as met, so it may not hold in full: REQ-210 WELCOME travels as a control record of type 5 in one fragment (to be rechecked on livedevelopment); REQ-6927 Push protocol 11 adds capability bit 26, MAGAZINE_SOUND_CAP, without which a receiver is sent no magazine music and no page magazine-music setting (tested, not recorded as met on livedevelopment).

Type 5. The body is one control message, encoded as a receiver's events are, 0xFF, a type, its fields, in at most 26 bytes, so that the record with its 8 bytes of frame is the 34 bytes of one fragment.

TypeNameFields
0x01WELCOMEversion uv, the version of the input protocol that HELLO named, 10 or 11; caps uv, a subset of the receiver's; and with RESUME in caps, session u8 (0 new, 1 resumed, others a protocol error), token of 16 bytes, and when resumed taken u16 big-endian, the input count the channel had taken
0x02 to 0x04NoneWithdrawn, once input modes. Reserved, and a record of one is ignored.
0x40 to 0x7FExtensionsA length, then a payload, skipped when unknown

Bytes left over, a body over 26 bytes, bit 16 set in caps, a bit no capability is, or SNAPSHOT and MAGAZINE_SOUND set together (capabilities) refuse the record. A capability above bit 27 would need a WELCOME of its own design. A resumed session restores the session's identity and its input count, and nothing of any page's local state.

5.8 The cursor record

DOC-1954 · reference · normative · NeoTeletext's own: no standard defines it · requirements REQ-195, REQ-196, REQ-209, REQ-212

Unfinished. The project's records do not show all of this as met, so it may not hold in full: REQ-195 The cursor record (to be rechecked on livedevelopment); REQ-196 Reader keeps the last cursor line of a TTI page (to be rechecked on livedevelopment); REQ-209 The cursor record carries the input count the channel has acted on (to be rechecked on livedevelopment); REQ-212 A receiver moves a viewer only on a REDIRECT record, never on a cursor record (to be rechecked on livedevelopment).

Type 4, always one fragment: 16 bytes, the frame and a body of 8 bytes.

Body byteFieldRange
0 and 1page, big-endian0x100 to 0x8FF
2 and 3acknowledged, big-endianThe input count acted on, modulo 65,536, or 0 for none yet
4row1 to 23, or 255 for no cursor. Row 0 is the header, and row 24 the Fastext row.
5column0 to 39
6reservedWritten 0, ignored when read
7flags4 BLOCK, a block rather than a bar. 1 and 2 are reserved, written 0 and ignored when read. Any other is refused.

No cursor requires column and flags 0. A record that breaks any rule is refused whole. A cursor is optional: a game sends none, or one with no cursor only to acknowledge. A receiver takes a cursor record wherever it comes, alone or in a message with the packets of an answer, and shows it only on the page it names, in a style no page can draw, and only while keys go to its channel.

A cursor record MUST NOT move a viewer, whatever page it names: one still in flight when a viewer selects another page names the page they left.

A page file may carry its cursor as a CU line, CU,row,column,width,flags[,acknowledged], in decimal, for the page that holds it. The reader keeps the last such line, and reports and drops a line it cannot read. width keeps its place and means nothing: it is read as a number and not kept. The engine's page encoder does not turn the line into a packet: a receiver reads it from the page it already has.

5.9 The index record

DOC-1955 · reference · normative · NeoTeletext's own: no standard defines it · requirements REQ-514, REQ-1477

Unfinished. The project's records do not show all of this as met, so it may not hold in full: REQ-514 `contents.txt` is read by a strict, bounded reader (to be rechecked on livedevelopment); REQ-1477 The server refuses, whole, a reply or index whose magazines and pages, or a reply whose selected sub-page, are not exactly shaped and bounded (to be rechecked on livedevelopment).

Type 6: the channel's magazines and pages, as a program gives them. A live channel has no contents.txt, and its index comes as these records, at connection and whenever it changes. Integers are big-endian. Text is a u16 byte length then that many bytes of UTF-8, with no control character and at most 120 characters, so at most 480 bytes.

BytesFieldRange
0 and 1generationAny: the same in every record of one sending, and another in the next, the sender counting on by one and wrapping
2 and 3part0 to parts - 1
4 and 5parts1 to 2,030: a record for each of the 2,022 pages and one for each magazine's name alone
6magazine1 to 8
7 onnameText, 0 to 120 characters: empty when it has none
ThenPagesZero or more, to the end of the body, in ascending page number
Field of a pageRange
page, u160x100 to 0x8FF, of the record's magazine, never a reserved number: mFD, mFE, mFF, 1BE or 1F0
subpages, u161 to 8,190: how many sub-pages the page has
title, text1 to 120 characters
section, text0 to 120 characters: the heading the page is listed under, empty for none

Splitting. A record holds one magazine's pages, as many as fit in 1,016 bytes of body, and a magazine with more goes on in the next record. The records of a sending are numbered in the order of their magazines and pages, so no page is in two records of one sending. A magazine's name is given in its first record of a sending, and the records after it give an empty name, which keeps the name given. A record may hold no pages, and then carries only the magazine's name.

Reassembling. A receiver keeps the index it has and the sending it is receiving.

  1. A record of the generation it is receiving, whose parts agrees with that sending's first record, adds its pages to the sending. A record of another generation begins a new sending, and the one in progress is abandoned.
  2. Each page a record lists is shown at once, added to the index or replacing what was there.
  3. When every part has arrived, the sending is the whole index, and every page and magazine it did not list is removed.
  4. A partial sending removes nothing.

For a viewer, a section begins wherever a page's section differs from the page before it.

5.10 The LOG record

DOC-1956 · reference · normative · NeoTeletext's own: no standard defines it · requirements REQ-190

Unfinished. The project's records do not show all of this as met, so it may not hold in full: REQ-190 A channel's log lines (to be rechecked on livedevelopment).

Type 7: a log line for the channel's author, as a TTI LG line holds one, shown only in a developer's view, never on a page.

BytesFieldRange
0levelE an error, W a warning, or I information
1 and 2page, big-endianThe page the line concerns, 0x100 to 0x8FF, or 0 for none
3 to the endtextUTF-8, 1 to 200 bytes, with no control character and no bidirectional formatting character

A receiver passes on at most 16 LOG records for each page frame it receives, and 16 before the first, and drops the rest, so that a channel cannot flood a console.

5.11 The LINKS record

DOC-1958 · reference · normative · NeoTeletext's own: no standard defines it · requirements REQ-1494

Unfinished. The project's records do not show all of this as met, so it may not hold in full: REQ-1494 A page's TTI Link Extension links travel as a LINKS record on data channel 12 (to be rechecked on main).

Type 9: a sub-page's Link Extension links, which packets cannot carry: key links to other services, to addresses and to the web, page-number links and text links. It holds every Link Extension link of the sub-page, the key links to its own service too, so that the links a receiver holds are exactly the page's. The page's Fastext links and row 24 still travel in its packets X/27/0 and X/24.

Integers are big-endian. A target is a u16 byte length, then 1 to 8,004 bytes of printable ASCII with no space and no comma, in any form the Link Extension allows.

BytesFieldRange
0 and 1page0x100 to 0x8FF: the sub-page's page
2 and 3sub0x0000 to 0x3F7E: its sub-code
4part0 to parts - 1
5parts1 to 21, the most links a sub-page has, 5 + 8 + 8
6keys0 to 5, then that many key links
Thennumbers0 to 8, then that many page-number links
Thentexts0 to 8, then that many text links, and nothing after
LinkFields
Key link (LN)key u8: R, G, Y, C or I; target; label: a u8 length, then 0 to 9 bytes of printable ASCII, at most 8 for a target in another service or at an address, and none for I
Page-number link (LK)number u16, a page number 0x100 to 0x8FF the page shows; target, never a web: one
Text link (LT)row u8, 1 to 23; column u8, 0 to 39; length u8, at least 1, with column + length at most 40; target

Bounds across the parts. Over all the parts of one sending, a sub-page has at most five key links, each key once and at most four of them coloured, at most eight page-number links, each number once, and at most eight text links. A record that would break one is refused.

Splitting. The links go in order, key links first, then page-number links, then text links, as many in each record as fit in 8,184 bytes of body. A link is never split.

What a receiver does. The server sends a sub-page's LINKS records straight after its frame, every time it sends the sub-page, whenever it has any Link Extension link. Part 0 replaces every link the receiver held for that page and sub-code, and later parts add to it. A sub-page sent without a LINKS record has no Link Extension links, and a receiver drops those it held for it. A receiver reads the links exactly as it reads a TTI file's LN, LK and LT lines.

5.12 The REGIS and NAPLPS records, types 14 and 17

DOC-6832 · reference · normative · NeoTeletext's own: no standard defines it · requirements REQ-6336, REQ-6408, REQ-6761

Unfinished. The project's records do not show all of this as met, so it may not hold in full: REQ-6408 A channel's NAPLPS for a sub-page is carried by the kit, the server and the engine and drawn by the browser in the page's place (to be rechecked on livedevelopment); REQ-6761 Capability bits REGIS_CAP (23) and NAPLPS_CAP (24, NAPLPS on the raster from line 20), and DRAWING_LINKS and REGIS_CURSOR naming NAPLPS objects too (PAR-1, PAR-2, RAS-9) (to be rechecked on livedevelopment).

Type 14, REGIS: bytes of a sub-page's ReGIS, the vector graphics language of DEC's VT330 and VT340 terminals as NeoTeletext's ReGIS v2 extends it, which a receiver draws on an 800 by 480 screen in place of the sub-page's teletext page. Type 17, NAPLPS: bytes of a sub-page's NAPLPS (ANSI X3.110-1983), which a receiver draws on the teletext raster in place of the sub-page's teletext page. The two bodies have one layout; the record's type says which language the bytes are.

Integers are big-endian.

BytesFieldRange
0 and 1page0x100 to 0x8FF: the sub-page's page
2 and 3sub0x0000 to 0x3F7E: its sub-code
4 and 5generationAny: which stream of this sub-page the bytes are of
6 to 9offsetWhere in that stream the bytes begin; offset plus the length of data MUST NOT pass 232 less one
10 to the enddata0 to 8,174 bytes of the stream: what a record's body of at most 8,184 bytes leaves after the fixed fields

One stream for each sub-page. A sub-page's picture is one stream of bytes, sent in as many records as it needs. A record of a new generation begins the stream again at offset 0: the receiver starts a new renderer for that page and sub-code, with nothing drawn. Within a generation each record's offset is where the last one ended; a receiver that finds a gap has lost a record, applies nothing more of that generation, and waits for the next. The record's reader does not read the bytes: the receiver's renderer bounds what they can cost.

Who is sent them. A channel sends REGIS records only to a receiver that agreed REGIS, bit 23, and NAPLPS records only to one that agreed NAPLPS, bit 24 (capabilities); a receiver that did not agree a picture's language is given the mosaic fallback instead. A picture's companions are DRAWING_LINKS and REGIS_CURSOR in either language and NAPLPS_OBJECTS in NAPLPS. Text in a picture is written in NeoTeletext's provided character sets: in ReGIS as alphabets 100 to 154, in NAPLPS by the private designations of the same sets.

In a static channel. A sub-page's picture records MAY follow its teletext packets in its own T42 file, as packets 4/31 on data channel 12: one stream of generation 1 from offset 0, at most 1,048,576 bytes of stream, then its NAPLPS_OBJECTS, DRAWING_LINKS and REGIS_CURSOR, under the file bounds of page folders and sub-page files.

5.13 The DRAWING_LINKS and REGIS_CURSOR records

DOC-6827 · reference · normative · NeoTeletext's own: no standard defines it · requirements REQ-6370, REQ-6371, REQ-6761, REQ-6767

Unfinished. The project's records do not show all of this as met, so it may not hold in full: REQ-6761 Capability bits REGIS_CAP (23) and NAPLPS_CAP (24, NAPLPS on the raster from line 20), and DRAWING_LINKS and REGIS_CURSOR naming NAPLPS objects too (PAR-1, PAR-2, RAS-9) (to be rechecked on livedevelopment).

Type 15, DRAWING_LINKS: the numbered drawings or objects of a sub-page's picture that are links, and where each leads. Type 16, REGIS_CURSOR: the drawing or object that is the sub-page's cursor, the mark that shows where typing goes, which the channel draws and moves and the receiver blinks. A number names a ReGIS numbered drawing when the sub-page's picture is ReGIS, and a NAPLPS object (NAPLPS objects) when it is NAPLPS: the bytes are the same for both, and which the number names is the sub-page's picture language.

Integers are big-endian. A target is a u16 byte length, then 1 to 8,004 bytes of printable ASCII with no space and no comma, in any form a text link's target takes.

BytesFieldRange
0 and 1page0x100 to 0x8FF: the sub-page's page
2 and 3sub0x0000 to 0x3F7E: its sub-code
4part0 to parts - 1
5parts1 to 64
6count0 to 64, then that many links, and nothing after
Each linknumber, targetnumber u16, 1 to 65,535, each once in the sending; target

REGIS_CURSOR's body is six bytes: page (2 bytes, 0x100 to 0x8FF), sub (2 bytes, 0x0000 to 0x3F7E) and number (2 bytes, 1 to 65,535, or 0 for no cursor). It carries no input count: the cursor record of type 4 goes on acknowledging input for the teletext page beneath the picture.

Bounds across the parts. Over the parts of one sending a sub-page has at most 64 drawing links, each number once. A link is never split: the links go in order, as many in each record as fit in 8,184 bytes of body.

What a receiver does. Part 0 replaces the drawing links the receiver held for that page and sub-code, later parts add to them, and a record of one part and no links removes them all. A receiver follows a press on a linked drawing or object itself, under the same rules as a text link: the destination shown while the pointer is on it, the dwell time, and the question before leaving the channel. The wire vectors records drawing_links and records regis_cursor of neoteletext-common's wire-vectors.tsv are a NAPLPS sub-page's object 301 leading to 302 and made its cursor.

In a rule table's group. A group MAY hold either record (groups and commands): a program's regis_links, naplps_links, regis_cursor and naplps_cursor without connections, page and sub, a DRAWING_LINKS command being one whole sending, part 0 of 1, within the command limit.

5.14 The PAINT record

DOC-7103 · reference · normative · NeoTeletext's own: no standard defines it · requirements REQ-7024, REQ-7025

Unfinished. The project's records do not show all of this as met, so it may not hold in full: REQ-7024 A page MAY state a line speed at which its NAPLPS or ReGIS v1 picture is painted, as if its bytes arrived over a serial line of that speed (tested, not recorded as met on main); REQ-7025 A page MAY state a default paint rate taken by every ReGIS v2 numbered drawing that sets none of its own (tested, not recorded as met on main).

Type 35, PAINT: how one generation of a sub-page's ReGIS or NAPLPS picture is painted, so that a picture can be shown arriving as it would over a serial line, and a ReGIS page's numbered drawings can paint gradually without each stating a rate. A channel sends it immediately before the first REGIS or NAPLPS record of the generation it names, in the same sending and inside the same atomic frame when one is open. It is defined by push protocol 11: a channel MUST NOT send it on a connection of version 10 (the session), where the picture is painted at once.

The body is exactly 14 bytes. Integers are big-endian.

BytesFieldRange
0 and 1page0x100 to 0x8FF: the sub-page's page
2 and 3sub0x0000 to 0x3F7E: its sub-code
4language1 ReGIS, 2 NAPLPS: the picture language, by the codes the SHEET record's kind uses (sprite sheets and the SHEET record)
5reserved0
6 and 7generationthe generation of the stream the values are for
8 to 11line_speed0 for none, else MIN_LINE_SPEED, 300, to MAX_LINE_SPEED, 115,200: bits a second
12 and 13default_rate0 for none, else 1 to MAX_DEFAULT_PAINT_RATE, 32,767; for ReGIS only

What a receiver refuses. A record of any other length, with a reserved byte that is not 0, with a language other than 1 or 2, with a line speed or a default rate outside its range, with a default rate for NAPLPS, or with both values 0 is refused whole, and the picture is then painted at once. A refused record ends nothing else: the stream's records that follow are read as usual.

What a receiver does. It keeps at most one pending PAINT record for each page, sub-code and language, and applies it when the generation it names starts; a record for a generation that never starts is dropped when another replaces it. Inside an atomic frame it is held with the rest of the frame. It is kept with the stream it belongs to, so a page shown again from what the receiver kept is painted the same way again.

  • Line speed. The receiver gives the generation's bytes to its renderer at the speed of a serial line of that many bits a second, each byte costing LINE_BITS_PER_BYTE, 10, bits (a start bit, eight data bits and a stop bit). On the presentation clock of 60 ticks a second, LINE_PACE_TICKS, 600, is the ticks' worth of bits in one second's bytes: in a run of t ticks the line carries t × line_speed ÷ 600 bytes, the remainder carried to the next run. A NAPLPS WAIT's time is added to the line's time. A generation with a line speed is presented from its first tick, not held until it is whole. Bytes that arrive while more than the renderer's hold limit, 262,144 bytes, wait to be drawn end the pacing, and everything held is drawn at once.
  • Default paint rate. A ReGIS numbered drawing that states no paint rate of its own (no T) is painted at this rate; a drawing that states T0 is painted at once, and one that states another rate keeps its own.

The viewer's choice. A receiver that offers its viewer a setting to paint drawings gradually, or that honours a request for reduced motion, draws everything at once when the setting is off or reduced motion is asked for; the painted trigger of the rule table (rules, triggers, keys and targets) then fires as soon as the bytes are drawn.

The record carries two numbers and no bytes for any renderer. The wire vector records paint of neoteletext-common's wire-vectors.tsv is a ReGIS picture of page 101, sub-code 0001, generation 1, at 1,200 bits a second with a default paint rate of 20.

5.15 The SUBPAGES record

DOC-1959 · reference · normative · NeoTeletext's own: no standard defines it · requirements REQ-1503

Unfinished. The project's records do not show all of this as met, so it may not hold in full: REQ-1503 The server sends a page's sub-page list as a SUBPAGES record, sub-codes in ascending order with 0000 first (to be rechecked on main).

Type 10: a page's list of sub-pages. Sub-pages are never sent with their page, so a receiver learns a page's list from this record, for the list, the count, the place shown, such as "3/12", and stepping. It is never the sub-pages themselves. It is sent when the connection selects the page or one of its sub-pages and does not hold the list's current version, and again whenever the list changes while the selection is the page or one of its sub-pages.

Integers are big-endian.

BytesFieldRange
0 and 1page0x100 to 0x8FF
2 and 3versionAny: the same in every record of one sending, and changed whenever the list changes
4 and 5part0 to parts - 1
6 and 7parts1 to 8,190
8 and 9count1 to 8,190: the page's sub-pages, the same in every record of the sending
ThenEntriesOne or more, to the end of the body, in the page's order

Each entry is sub u16, a sub-code 0x0000 to 0x3F7E, each at most once in the list, then title: a u8 byte length and 0 to 160 bytes of UTF-8, at most 40 characters, with no control character, empty for none.

Splitting. The entries go in the page's order, ascending sub-code with 0000 first when present, as many in each record as fit in 1,016 bytes of body, at least six, and an entry is never split.

Reassembling, as the index: a record of another version of the page begins a new sending. A sending is complete when every part has arrived and its entries number count, and then it is the page's whole list. A partial sending shows what it has and removes nothing.

Rests on: EN 300 706 V1.2.1 clause 3.1 Definitions; EN 300 706 V1.2.1 clause A.1 Page numbering

5.16 The REDIRECT record

DOC-1960 · reference · normative · NeoTeletext's own: no standard defines it · requirements REQ-212, REQ-1688

Unfinished. The project's records do not show all of this as met, so it may not hold in full: REQ-212 A receiver moves a viewer only on a REDIRECT record, never on a cursor record (to be rechecked on livedevelopment); REQ-1688 A program's redirect may name another channel, which the browser follows after the redirect notice (to be rechecked on main).

Type 11: what a program sends to move a connection's viewer to another page of the channel, or to another channel. It is the only thing that moves a viewer. An HTTP redirect from a web server is another thing, and is not carried here.

The body is one address, as an HTTP Location is, of printable ASCII with no space and no fragment. It is either a place of this channel, 302 or 302/0002, with a query when the selection it moves keeps one, at most 8,009 bytes; or a whole address, an http or https address the strict address parser accepts, at most 8,000 bytes. A place on a reserved page is refused.

  • A place. The server sends the record and records the page as the connection's selection, with its query, exactly as it would a SELECT, and the program is then sent selected for it. A receiver opens that page and sub-page, whether or not its page has the focus, and sends SELECT for it, with the query. A redirect to a sub-page names the selection as it stands, so that SELECT repeats it and asks for nothing more. A redirect to a page, sub-code 3F7F, is answered with a sub-page, which then is the selection, so the receiver's SELECT of the page is a new one: the program hears selected again, and the receiver is sent that sub-page again, whole.
  • A whole address. The server sends the record and changes nothing else: the selection stands until the receiver leaves. A receiver that opens channels puts the address through its own address rules, which alone decide: a redirect leads only to an http or https address, never a local file, a web: hand-off or the receiver's own pages. It shows a redirect notice, and then opens the address as another channel. A receiver that cannot open channels says that the channel redirected and to where, and stays.

The viewer's own choice overrides a redirect, and a receiver bounds how many redirects it follows in a row with no input from the viewer.

5.17 The DENIED record

DOC-1961 · reference · normative · NeoTeletext's own: no standard defines it · requirements REQ-1481

Unfinished. The project's records do not show all of this as met, so it may not hold in full: REQ-1481 A selection the program does not answer in time ends with DENIED 503 and the connection stays open (to be rechecked on livedevelopment).

Type 12: a selection refused by the channel's program, at once, or a program that did not answer by the deadline. It gives every selection a defined answer, as a status gives a web request one. Integers are big-endian.

BytesFieldRange
0 and 1statusA real HTTP status number: 403 not allowed, 404 no such page, 429 a limit reached, or 503 the channel's program is not answering
2 to the endplaceThe place refused, as SELECT carried it with no query, or as the selection then stood, so a page already answered is named by its sub-page, 100/0000, at most 8 bytes of printable ASCII, or nothing when the whole channel is unavailable

The connection stays open. A receiver says so to the viewer in words of its own, and takes the next selection as usual. A connection with no selection, whose program did not answer, is sent DENIED 503 with no place.

5.18 What arrives as one unit

DOC-1962 · reference · normative · NeoTeletext's own: no standard defines it · requirements REQ-200, REQ-1494, REQ-1503

Unfinished. The project's records do not show all of this as met, so it may not hold in full: REQ-200 Input is sent as one ordered stream of raw UTF-8 text and 0xFF-framed events (to be rechecked on livedevelopment); REQ-1494 A page's TTI Link Extension links travel as a LINKS record on data channel 12 (to be rechecked on main); REQ-1503 The server sends a page's sub-page list as a SUBPAGES record, sub-codes in ascending order with 0000 first (to be rechecked on main).

A receiver applies these whole, or not at all.

  • A page frame and its links: the frame's packets, then that sub-page's LINKS records when it has Link Extension links. The next frame, or a frame with no LINKS record, is what says it has none. A frame is applied before its LINKS records arrive, and a sub-page shows no Link Extension links until they do.
  • A sending of the index, or of a SUBPAGES list: whole when every part has arrived. A partial one shows what it has and removes nothing.
  • A LINKS sending: part 0 replaces what was held, and later parts add to it.
  • A record of several fragments: whole by its CRC, or discarded.
  • A WebSocket message of the input stream: whole items, read alone.

Nothing else is a unit. A selection's sub-page and its SUBPAGES record may arrive in either order, and a receiver holds neither back for the other.

5.19 The wire vectors

DOC-1963 · reference · normative · NeoTeletext's own: no standard defines it · requirements REQ-200, REQ-1462

Unfinished. The project's records do not show all of this as met, so it may not hold in full: REQ-200 Input is sent as one ordered stream of raw UTF-8 text and 0xFF-framed events (to be rechecked on livedevelopment); REQ-1462 Server sends only valid packets downstream (to be rechecked on main).

These are the protocol's byte-level examples, in hexadecimal. Their source is the file wire-vectors.tsv of neoteletext-common, at push protocol version 10: one row a line, of four columns separated by a tab, the row's kind, its name, its value and what it means. The engine writes the file (cargo xtask) and reads and writes every row; the server and the browser check their own code against the same file, and the server runs every row against a channel whole. A new implementation SHOULD run the same rows. The file's comment lines say what each kind of row holds.

KindWhat a row holds
versionwhat both sides must say: the input protocol's version and the subprotocol
closea WebSocket close code and what a receiver does on it: stop or retry
inputone message of the input stream at the top level: HELLO, SELECT, RESIZE, and extensions a receiver skips
refusedbytes a reader MUST refuse, among them a viewer's input at the top level of the stream
record, recordsone record of the record frame, or several, each as its 42-byte packets 4/31 on data channel 12: WELCOME, CURSOR, DENIED, REDIRECT, and the records of the rule table and of animation (RULES, RULES_QUERY, the six command records, ANIMATE, SPRITES, NAPLPS_OBJECTS, SHEET, FRAME)
rulesa page's table image, the default table with and without the wheel
commandthe body of one of the six command records as a group holds it, each VARIABLE operation with each operand kind among them
rule_event, page_state, rules_faultone input event of the rule table, as a receiver writes it
objecta local sound's OBJECT record, as the engine and as the server write it

What both sides must say.

NameValueMeans
input10HELLO's and WELCOME's version
subprotocolneottx.10Sec-WebSocket-Protocol, asked for and echoed

Close codes, and what a receiver does: broke_protocol 4000, stop; wrong_version 4001, stop; unnamed_stop 4050, stop; restarting 4100, retry; unnamed_retry 4150, retry; normal 1000, retry; above_the_ranges 4200, retry.

5.20 Decided, not built in full: titles in every character set

DOC-2269 · reference · informative · NeoTeletext's own: no standard defines it · requirements REQ-2194

Unfinished. The project's records do not show all of this as met, so it may not hold in full: REQ-2194 Channel and list titles carry every character of every NeoTeletext character set as UTF-8 (not implemented on main).

A channel's name, a magazine's name, a section heading, a page's title and a sub-page's title are not teletext page content: they travel in records and files and a receiver draws them outside the page, in its tab and lists. So no teletext character set limits them, and the design is that each may hold any Unicode text but control characters, as UTF-8, everywhere it travels.

What holds today. The index record carries magazine names, headings and page titles as UTF-8, up to 120 characters each, and channel.ttx's name is UTF-8 up to 64 bytes.

What is not built. The SUBPAGES record and a static channel's contents.txt still take printable ASCII alone, so a sub-page titled in Russian or Japanese arrives as spaces or is refused. The design gives every such text one rule, defined once and implemented once in the engine: a 2-byte big-endian length in bytes and UTF-8 in a record; invalid UTF-8 and control characters refused; bidirectional controls and other invisible format controls removed when read; normalised to Unicode Normalization Form C when read; and bounded in characters and in bytes at four bytes a character, 120 characters for titles and headings, sub-page titles included, and 64 for the channel's name, a text over its bound cut at a character boundary. The receiver is to draw every character of every NeoTeletext set in these titles from fonts it carries itself, so they look the same on every machine, with right-to-left titles laid out by the Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm and a title too long for its row cut with an ellipsis at a grapheme cluster boundary.

5.21 Decided, not built: changing a live channel's attributes while viewers are connected

DOC-2268 · reference · informative · NeoTeletext's own: no standard defines it · requirements REQ-2195

Unfinished. The project's records do not show all of this as met, so it may not hold in full: REQ-2195 Live channel attributes change while viewers are connected (not implemented on main).

Not built. Today a channel's attributes, everything about it that is not a page, come from channel.ttx, read once when a receiver opens the channel, so nothing changes them while a viewer is connected. The design lets a live channel's program change every one of them at any time, for the connections it names.

  • The standard's packets where the standard has one, so that a recording means the same to any teletext decoder. A magazine's default character set and region is a new packet M/29/0 (EN 300 706 clause 9.5.1), which a receiver already applies above channel.ttx's region; this is how a channel gives each magazine its own language. The initial page is packet 8/30 Format 1, bytes 7 to 12 (clause 9.8.1); the latest on the connection wins over the file, for the page shown when no page is named and for the Home key.
  • A CHANNEL record for the rest, record type 13 in the record frame on data channel 12: name, region, services, aliases and any attribute added to channel.ttx later. Each record is whole, with a generation number, never a patch; an attribute it leaves out takes the file's value. Every value is checked by the same reader as channel.ttx, with the same bounds and refusals, so a record can never say what the file could not; a record that fails is discarded whole and counted as an invalid packet. refresh is not carried, since only a static channel has it.
  • Input is not an attribute. A page asks for the viewer's input with its own rule table, which the server sends at every selection of the page, so neither channel.ttx nor a CHANNEL record says anything of input, and nothing here changes what a channel is sent.
  • Precedence, highest first: the page's own packets, its magazine's M/29, the latest CHANNEL record, channel.ttx, the receiver's own settings. The viewer's own choices stand above all of them.
  • For the connection. The server keeps no content, so a record holds for the connection it was sent on, and a program sends it again after WELCOME, as it sends the index. Different connections may be given different attributes, such as a name in each viewer's language.
  • The program's side is a new message, channel, which the server checks with the same reader, encodes, checks again by reading what it wrote, and sends.

A static channel changes its attributes by changing channel.ttx, which a receiver reads again when it reopens the channel. Whether the engine applies a changed M/29/0 and packet 8/30's initial page on a live channel today has not been checked.

Rests on: EN 300 706 V1.2.1 clause 9.5.1 Packet M/29/0; EN 300 706 V1.2.1 clause 9.8.1 Packet 8/30 Format 1

6 The page rule table

DOC-6581 · section

6.1 A page asks for input with its rule table

DOC-6583 · concept · normative · NeoTeletext's own: no standard defines it · requirements REQ-6523, REQ-6528

Unfinished. The project's records do not show all of this as met, so it may not hold in full: REQ-6523 The browser sends the server no input event for a page unless the page's rule table asks for it (tested, not recorded as met on main).

A page — one page number and one sub-code together (a sub-page is a page) — may carry a rule table: a bounded, declarative list of rules, each binding one to four events (a key, a pointer action on a target, a timer, the page opening or closing, a condition becoming true, a cue in a playing sound) to one group of protocol commands, which the receiver holds and applies itself. A command is an ordinary record of the push protocol, the same bytes a server sends to play a sound or a note on a local sound, to show, hide, move or re-look an object, to place sprites, to change a variable, to start a timer or a sequence, or to report to the channel (groups and commands). A receiver handles each event of the open page the moment it arrives, applying every command of the groups it runs at once, and runs what time drives on a clock of sixty ticks a second (handlings), so that sound and picture answer the viewer with no round trip to the server.

The table is the only way a page asks for the viewer's input. Push protocol version 10 has these rules:

  • A receiver MUST NOT send its channel any event of the viewer's input on a page (a key, text, a paste, a composition, a pointer press, release or move, the wheel, a touch, a hover, a pick, a gain or loss of the keyboard) unless a rule of that page's table fired on that event and its group, in that event's own handling, applied a REPORT command of the firing. A group run by a timer, a sequence, a cue, the page's opening or closing, a condition becoming true or a command of the server's reports no input event at all. A page with no table is sent nothing of what its viewer does. It is still shown, its links work, its sound plays, the records the server sends it that need no table (CONTROL, ANIMATE, SPRITES, NAPLPS_OBJECTS) are applied, and SELECT still tells the channel which page and sub-page the tab shows.
  • The viewer's input travels only inside a RULE_EVENT (RULE_EVENT). A server MUST treat KEY, MOUSE, WHEEL, TOUCH, PASTE, COMPOSE, FOCUS_IN, FOCUS_OUT, HOVER, PICK, DRAWING_HOVER or raw text at the top level of the input stream as a protocol error and close the connection with code 4000, and a receiver MUST never write one there. HELLO, RESIZE, SELECT, RESUME and viewer state's messages stay at the top level: they are the session, not the viewer's input to a page.
  • Only the open page is evaluated and given input: the one page of the active tab that keys would go to. A page that is merely visible elsewhere, or in a tab that is not the active one, is paused (the lifetime of local state): it evaluates nothing, plays no local sound and is given no input.
  • A receiver keeps for itself, whatever a table says: a key or click made with the receiver's own modifier, and every key its own strip and dialogs have; a press and release on a link the page declares, which it follows itself; the wheel over a page whose page number has more than one sub-code, unless the pointer is inside the target of a wheel rule of the table; and everything typed or clicked outside the open page's picture.
  • The descriptor's push.input and push.wheel are withdrawn: a server MUST NOT write them, and a receiver MUST read past them whatever value they hold.

A table is event binding, never executable content. It has no loop, no jump, no conditional inside a group, no multiplication, division, bit operation or random number, no computed address (a variable choosing a target, a sound, a group, a timer, a sequence or another variable), no call of a routine, no text processing and no command that changes a table, a group, a sequence or a row. Its only arithmetic is the saturating addition and subtraction of 32-bit integers in the variable command and in a command's value held to its field's range (binding rows and amounts), and no command can make a rule fire while it is being applied. The receiver's own timekeeping (when an every trigger is due, a timer's phase, a sequence's start on a beat) takes a remainder of its own count of ticks by a period that is a constant of the table; no table asks for it. A table that breaks any rule or limit of this part is refused whole, never accepted in part or repaired (the limits).

6.2 Handlings: each event at once in arrival order, and a tick step for what time drives

DOC-6584 · reference · normative · NeoTeletext's own: no standard defines it · requirements REQ-6526, REQ-6534

Unfinished. The project's records do not show all of this as met, so it may not hold in full: REQ-6534 The decoder MUST handle the open page's rule table events at once and apply its groups' commands, and the trusted core MUST gate every report (tested, not recorded as met on livedevelopment).

The clock. A receiver runs an open page's tick step once for each tick of its presentation clock, 60 ticks a second: tick n is due n × 50,000 ÷ 3 microseconds (rounded down) after the clock's start, so that ticks are never skipped or repeated. A page's first tick step is page tick 0, at the first clock tick after the page was opened in the view and its table decoded; each later clock tick is the next page tick, an unsigned 32-bit number that stops at 4,294,967,295. When the receiver is late it runs each due tick step in order, at most MAX_CATCH_UP_TICKS in one wake, and when more are due it moves the clock's start later by the ticks it will not run, so that page time slows and no page tick is ever skipped. While the page is paused no tick step is run.

Handlings. The evaluator does all its work in handlings, one at a time and never interleaved: the handling of one event, or the tick step of one page tick. Every handling has exactly two phases. Decide: the handling's firings are determined — each rule, in rule order, and within a rule each of its rows in row order, that the event or the tick step fires, its condition read against the page's state as it stands at the start of the handling. Apply: the group of each firing is run, in the order the firings were decided, and each command takes effect at once, as it is reached. No command applied in a handling changes which rules that handling fires: there is no cascade within a handling. What a command changes is seen by the conditions of later handlings, and within one run a later command reads what an earlier one wrote. A rule, or one row of it, fires at most once in a handling, however many of its triggers the event or the tick step matches. An event's decide phase keeps at most MAX_RULE_ROWS firings, a tick step's at most MAX_RULE_ROWS plus MAX_SEQUENCES × MAX_SEQUENCE_STEPS; a firing beyond, which only a trigger on any control or object in a rule with rows can cause, is dropped and counted.

Events. An event is an input event of the viewer's for the open page; a record the server sent directly for the page that the evaluator carries out (VARIABLE, TIMER, REPORT, RUN, SEQUENCE, and the state query RULES_QUERY); or a cue heard. The evaluator handles each event as soon as it reaches it, in arrival order, with nothing waiting for a tick:

  1. An event belongs to the page tick of the last tick step run. One that arrives before tick step 0 waits and is handled at once after it, belonging to page tick 0, so that a page's opening group runs first.
  2. An input event first updates the input state (which keys and buttons are down, where the pointer is and which targets it is inside), then its input triggers are matched. A cue is matched against the cue triggers. A record of the server's has one firing, the record itself, applied as a command (a RUN runs its group in place). A state query is answered at once from the state as it stands.
  3. The per-tick budgets. An event is handled in tick n only when fewer than MAX_EVENTS_PER_TICK events have been handled in it, and only when, with the commands of its own firings (each run's count of commands being a constant of the table), the tick's commands stay within MAX_EVENT_COMMANDS_PER_TICK and its REPORT commands within MAX_EVENT_REPORTS_PER_TICK. The first event handled in a tick is always handled. An event that does not fit leaves no trace (the change it made to the input state is put back), and it and every event after it wait, in arrival order, in one queue of at most MAX_QUEUED_EVENTS; they are handled at once after the next tick step, under that tick's budget. An event that arrives at a full queue is dropped and counted (RULES_FAULT code 4); none is dropped while the queue has room.
  4. When the page loses the keyboard, the pointer leaves, the page is paused or it closes, the receiver gives the evaluator a release, marked lost, for every key and button still down and a leave for every target the pointer was inside, each handled at once whatever the budgets, after the events already waiting, so that key_up, release and leave rules fire and no note is left sounding.

The records a receiver applies whether or not the page has a table (CONTROL, LOCAL_MIDI, ANIMATE, SPRITES, NAPLPS_OBJECTS) are not events: they are applied on arrival, between handlings, as changes to the world the evaluator reads.

The tick step of page tick t is one handling, whose decide phase determines its firings in exactly this order: (1) open, at page tick 0 only; (2) timers, the page timer first and then t0 to t7, each rule whose every or after trigger on a running timer is due; (3) sequences, 0 to 7: a sequence waiting to start at t becomes running, and each running sequence's steps whose offset equals its position; (4) becomes: each rule, and each of its rows, whose condition holds now and did not at its previous check. The apply phase then runs the decided groups in that order, and after them (5) each sequence that was running when the tick step began, and that no command of the tick step stopped or started again, advances, and (6) each cycling object whose frame is due advances. The waiting events are then handled. The per-tick budgets do not apply to a tick step.

Close. When the page is closed while its connection stands, the evaluator handles the lost releases, then runs one close handling, whose firings are the close rules whose condition holds; events still waiting are dropped and counted. No close handling is run on a disconnect.

Outputs. Every output of a handling leaves at once, in the order its command was applied: a sound command to the sound output stage, a report to the receiver's trusted part, the answer to a state query. A change to the picture is drawn at the next display frame from the state then current, so that several changes before one frame cost one repaint.

One state, read as it stands. The evaluator keeps one copy of the page's rule state and changes it in place: a condition reads it as it stands at the start of its handling, a command as it stands when the command is applied. What the evaluator reads but does not own — a target's state, the sound on each audio channel, a synthesizer's tracked values, the newest metered values — changes only between handlings. A recording of a page's inputs, each with its place among the tick steps (the engine keys it by the count of tick steps run), replayed in that order gives the same result on every run: wall-clock time within a tick affects no outcome.

6.3 Rules, triggers, keys and targets

DOC-6585 · reference · normative · NeoTeletext's own: no standard defines it · requirements REQ-6526, REQ-6613

A rule is 1 to MAX_TRIGGERS_PER_RULE triggers, any of which fires it; a condition, or none (conditions); optionally a run of binding rows (binding rows); and the number of one group of the same table, which it runs when it fires. It has no list of actions of its own, no echo flag and no enabled flag: a page that has sets of rules for different times expresses it as a mode, a variable that each rule of a set tests in its condition and that a group changes. A rule with a becomes trigger has exactly that one trigger and MUST have a condition. A table holds 0 to MAX_RULES rules, numbered 0 to 63 in the order written, which is rule order. Triggers that belong to different handlings (a key and a timer, say) each fire the rule in their own handling, so a rule may fire several times in one tick.

CodeTriggerFires whenFields
1keya key matching the key set is pressed; with repeat, also on each automatic repeatkey set, repeat, by_row, modifier mask and value
2key_upa key matching the key set is released, or lostkey set, by_row, modifier mask and value
3pressa pointer button or a touch contact goes down inside the targettarget, button
4releasea button or contact that went down inside the target comes up, wherever the pointer then istarget, button
5enterthe pointer comes inside the targettarget
6leavethe pointer goes outside the target, or leaves the pagetarget
7openpage tick 0's tick stepnone
8closethe page is closed while its connection standsnone
9becomesat a tick step, the rule's condition holds and did not at its previous checknone: the condition is the rule's
10everyeach ticks ticks after the timer started, while it runstimer, ticks
11afteronce, ticks ticks after the timer startedtimer, ticks
12texttext arrives that is not a key: a paste, an input method's composition or its committed textnone
13movethe pointer moves to another pixel inside the target; with held, only while a button is downtarget, held
14wheelthe wheel turns with the pointer inside the targettarget
15focusthe page gains the keyboardnone
16blurthe page loses the keyboardnone
21cuea cue of the sound playing on an audio channel is heard (cue points)audio channel 0 to 3, cue number or any

Codes 17 to 20 are refused and never reused: a long press is a key rule that starts a timer, a key_up rule that stops it and an after rule on the timer; a double press is a key rule that sets a variable and starts a timer when the variable is 0, a second key rule that acts when it is 1, and an after rule that sets it back. Triggers 1 to 6 and 12 to 16 are input triggers, fired in an input event's handling; 21 in a cue's; 7, 9, 10 and 11 in the tick step; 8 in the close handling. A button is 0 (left, a touch contact or a pen touching), 1 (middle), 2 (right) or 255 (any). The modifier mask and value are the input protocol's modifier bits (KEY): a trigger matches when (mods AND mask) = value, and mask 0 ignores modifiers. ticks is 1 to MAX_TIMER_TICKS.

Key sets. A key set is any key, or 1 to MAX_KEYS_PER_TRIGGER keys, each a character key (the Unicode scalar value the active layout gives the key without Shift, exactly the KEY event's key when it is a character; letters in lower case), a named key (a functional key by its code in the input protocol's table of keys) or a physical key (the key that carries the given character on a United States layout, whatever the active layout: the KEY event's base when it has one, else its key). A key event matches a set when it matches any member. In a rule that names rows, a key set MAY be given one key a row (by_row): it then holds exactly as many keys as the rule names rows, and the row at place r matches the key at place r and no other.

Targets. A target is a kind and a 16-bit number: kind 0, the page's whole picture (number 0); kind 1, a teletext control of the page, 1 to 32, numbered from 1 in the order the page declares them, or 0 for any control; kind 2, an animation object (a teletext sprite, a ReGIS numbered drawing or a NAPLPS object), 1 to 65,535, or 0 for any object; kind 3, a rectangle the table declares, 0 to MAX_RECTS less one. "Any" is allowed only in press, release, enter, leave, move and wheel; it fires once for each control or object concerned, and the firing's target names which. In a rule that names rows, a trigger's target number MAY be a signed 16-bit constant plus the row's p. Inside is decided thus: the page, always; a control, when the pointer's cell is one of its cells; a ReGIS numbered drawing, when the picture's pick record names that drawing, or one that has it as an ancestor, at the pointer's pixel, and it is detectable; a teletext sprite or a NAPLPS object, when it is shown, detectable and its bounding rectangle holds the pointer's pixel; a rectangle, when it holds the pointer's pixel. One pointer event may be inside several targets, and every rule it matches fires, in rule order. enter and leave fire on any pointer event that carries a position when the set of targets under the pointer has changed; move fires only on a move to another pixel. A target that does not exist is never inside and reads as not shown. The pointer is followed inside at most MAX_POINTER_OBJECTS objects at once.

Rectangles and the grid. A table MAY declare 0 to MAX_RECTS rectangles, each x, y, width and height (0 to 65,535, width and height at least 1) in the pixels of the page's picture, origin at the top left: a teletext page is 480 by 500 dots (a cell 12 by 20); a NAPLPS picture is the same 480 by 500 dots of the teletext raster, drawn on rows 1 to 23 (lines 20 to 479) with rows 0 and 24 the teletext page's own, and its pointer's place, rectangles and objects are those dots; a ReGIS picture is 800 by 480 pixels. A rectangle partly outside the picture is cut to it.

becomes is an edge. Each becomes rule keeps one bit for itself, or one for each of its rows, false when the page opens. At each tick step's becomes place the condition is checked once against the state as it stands; the rule (or row) fires when it holds and the bit is false, and the bit is then set to the result. A condition that already holds at page tick 0 fires at tick 0, and a change an event's group makes is first seen at the next tick step's check.

6.4 Binding rows, and amounts: a rule as a template, and a variable as a command's value

DOC-6683 · concept · normative · NeoTeletext's own: no standard defines it · requirements REQ-6612, REQ-6613

Binding rows. A table MAY hold 0 to MAX_ROWS rows, numbered from 0 in the order written, each exactly one signed 32-bit constant, the row's parameter p. A rule MAY name a run of rows by its first row and a count (at least 1, within the table's rows), and two rules MAY name the same rows. Such a rule is a template that the receiver holds and matches once for each of its rows, in row order, the row standing in these places and no others:

  1. a key set given one key a row (by_row) of a key or key_up trigger: the set holds exactly as many keys as the rule names rows, and the row at place r among the rule's rows matches the set's key at place r and no other;
  2. the number of a trigger's target, given as a signed 16-bit constant to which p is added, which for every row the rule names MUST give a valid number for the target's kind (a control 1 to 32, an object 1 to 65,535, a rectangle the table has), checked when the table is decoded;
  3. the constant of a comparison in the rule's condition, to which p is added with saturation;
  4. an amount in a command of the group the rule runs, and of every group that group runs, whose source is p or the firing's row.

An event fires each row whose triggers, so given, it matches and for which the condition holds, each firing being one run of the rule's group with that row's p in force. A rule without rows runs its group with p 0, and a sequence started by a command of a run keeps the p in force. Rows are constants of the table: nothing changes them. A value a row needs beyond its one parameter is derived from it as a constant plus p (a drawing 41 + p for note p), from the row's place as a constant plus the firing's row (a meter's segment 301 + row), or from the row's place in a by_row key set. The sum, over a table's rules, of the rows each names (a rule without rows counting one) is at most MAX_RULE_ROWS, the most firings one event can cause.

Amounts. A command in a group MAY carry up to MAX_COMMAND_BINDINGS bindings. A binding names one field of the command and one source, and means: when the command runs, the field's value is the constant written in the command's body plus the source's value, added as signed 32-bit integers with saturation, and then held to the field's valid range (below the least becomes the least, above the greatest the greatest). The command is then applied exactly as if the server had sent it with that value.

Source byteSourceValue
0x10 to 0x1Fa variable v0 to v15its value as it stands when the command is applied
0x20the row parameter pthe p in force; 0 when none
0x30 to 0x33a value of the firing: the key, the target, the row, the cueas the firing gives it; 0 when there is none

Source bytes 0x21 to 0x23 are refused. The fields that take a binding are exactly these, and a binding of any other field refuses the table:

RecordField codeFieldValid rangeSources
LOCAL_MIDI1data 1 (the key, the controller or the program)0 to 127any
LOCAL_MIDI2data 2 (the velocity or the controller's value; not with program change)0 to 127any
LOCAL_MIDI3the 14-bit pitch bend value (status 0xEn only)0 to 16,383any
CONTROL1gain0 to 100any
CONTROL2fade, in milliseconds0 to 10,000any
ANIMATE, move2, 3x, y−32,768 to 32,767any
ANIMATE, frame4frame0 to 15any
ANIMATE, look5look0 to 3any
ANIMATE, order6order within the layer−128 to 127any
ANIMATE, cycle7period, in ticks1 to 3,600any
ANIMATE, every operation1the target's number1 to 32 for a control, 1 to 65,535 for an objectthe row's p (0x20), the firing's target (0x31) or the firing's row (0x32), never a variable

A binding's item byte is the place of the operation within an ANIMATE record, from 0, and 0 for every other record. A field has at most one binding. The target's number is an identity, not a quantity: it is not held to a range (a number outside its range makes that one operation do nothing and be counted), and it never takes a variable, because a variable choosing which object is acted on would be a computed address. No audio channel, handle, generation, page, sub-code, status byte, group, timer, sequence, variable designator, layer, flag or count takes a binding. VARIABLE has its own operands and takes none; TIMER, REPORT, RUN, SEQUENCE, SPRITES and NAPLPS_OBJECTS take none, and a record the server sends directly has none. A value that needs two sources (a note that is a row's p plus an octave variable) is made by VARIABLE commands first: set v2 to the firing's p, add v0, then the note's key is 0 plus v2.

6.5 The sixteen variables, the eight timers, conditions and the values they read

DOC-6586 · reference · normative · NeoTeletext's own: no standard defines it · requirements REQ-6526, REQ-6527

Unfinished. The project's records do not show all of this as met, so it may not hold in full: REQ-6527 The audio crates MUST make synthesizer state readable to page rules and MUST provide the local sound: parameter tables, envelope meter, voice peak, pulled voice (to be rechecked on livedevelopment).

Variables. Every page has exactly VARIABLES variables, designated v0 to v15 in every message and numbered 0 to 15 in every record. A table declares none and names none. Each is a signed 32-bit integer and nothing else, zero when the page opens; every operation on one saturates at −2,147,483,648 and 2,147,483,647 and is computed without overflow. They are changed only by the VARIABLE command (the six command records), are local to the page in its view, and are never shared between pages, sub-pages, tabs or channels.

Timers. Every page has exactly TIMERS timers, t0 to t7 (numbered 0 to 7), declared by no table and all stopped when the page opens, and the page timer (identifier 255, designated page), which always runs since page tick 0 and cannot be started or stopped. A TIMER start applied in a handling of page tick t makes a timer running since tick t + 1, replacing any earlier start; a stop stops it. With e the present page tick less the start tick, an after N trigger is due when e = N, and an every N trigger when e > 0 and e is a multiple of N: those ticks are the timer's expiries of a period of N.

Conditions. A condition is a tree of at most MAX_CONDITION_NODES nodes, of which at most MAX_CONDITION_TERMS are terms, with operators nested at most MAX_CONDITION_DEPTH deep: and and or (2 to MAX_AND_OR_CHILDREN children), not (one child); and the terms compare (a value, one of ==, !=, <, <=, >, >=, and a signed 32-bit constant, to which the row's p MAY be added in a rule that names rows), in range (low ≤ value ≤ high), in set (1 to MAX_SET_MEMBERS constants), overlaps (two targets whose bounding rectangles share at least one pixel) and inside (the first target's bounding rectangle lies wholly within the second's). Every comparison is of a value with a constant of the table; two values are never compared with each other and nothing is computed from them. overlaps and inside name a control, an object or a rectangle first and any target second, never "any" or the row's p; a control's rectangle is its cells in dots, an object's its renderer's bounding rectangle as it stands, and a target that does not exist or is not shown has none, so a test that names it is false.

Values. Every value is a signed 32-bit integer, named in a record by 8 bytes: a space byte, a byte a and three 16-bit fields b, c, d, every unused field 0. A value that cannot be read (no sound on the channel, another family's sound, a property the family does not have) reads as 0, and a property such as playing or exists tells 0 from absent. Every value is read as it stands when it is read.

SpaceValues
1, variablesa the variable, 0 to 15
2, key and pointer statea 1 a character key, 2 a named key, 3 a physical key, with the key's 32-bit code in b (high half) and c (low half): 1 while down. a 4 a pointer button, b 0 to 2: 1 while down over the page. a 5 the pointer, b 0 over the page (1 or 0), 1 its x pixel, 2 its y pixel. a 6 the count of keys down, 0 to 16. At most MAX_KEYS_DOWN keys are tracked as down
3, timersa the timer, 0 to 7 or 255; b 0 running (1 or 0), 1 elapsed ticks since its start (0 while stopped), 2 phase in a period P given in c (high) and d (low), 1 to MAX_TIMER_TICKS: the elapsed ticks less the greatest multiple of P not above them, so 0 at each expiry of that period (0 while stopped)
4, target statea the target's kind (1 control, 2 object), b its number, c the property: 0 exists, 1 shown, 2 frame (0 to 15), 3 x, 4 y (an object's position in its renderer's units; a control's first column and row), 5 the look in force (0 to 3), 6 layer, 7 order, 8 cycling, 9 the pointer inside
5, a sound on an audio channela the audio channel, 0 to 3; b 0 playing (1 while any sound plays on it in this view), 1 level (its output level over the last sixtieth of a second, 0 to 255, linear, 255 full scale, measured before the viewer's volume and mute), 2 handle (−1 when none), 3 gain as last commanded (0 to 100), 4 local (1 while the sound is a local sound)
6, a synthesizer's statea the audio channel; b the family expected, its codec code in the high byte (12 the synth6581 family, 13 synth7, 14 the synth106 family, 15 synthD, 16 the synth53 family, 17 synth8, 18 synth80) and its variant in the low byte (0, or 1 for synth8580, synth60 and synth52, 2 for synth51); c the part's MIDI channel less one in its high byte and the class in its low byte; d the index. Classes: 0 program; 1 notes (keys down on the part); 2 note (1 while key d is down); 3 velocity of key d's note on; 4 field, the present value of the family's patch field numbered d, on its own integer scale; 5 envelope_stage of the part's newest voice (0 idle, 1 attack, 2 decay, 3 sustain, 4 release); 6 envelope_level, 0 to 255; 7 voices not idle; 8 controller d's last value; 9 bend, 0 to 16,383, 8,192 at rest. A sound not of the named family and variant reads 0 in every class
7, the firinga 0 key (the code of the key whose event fired the rule), 1 target (the number of the control, object or rectangle the pointer event was inside), 2 row (the place of the firing row within the rule's rows), 3 cue (the number of the cue that fired it), 4 p (the row parameter in force); each 0 when there is none. In a command they are those of the run's firing, a nested run having its caller's; a sequence's run has its held p and 0 for the rest, a run of a server's record 0 for all. a 5 to 7 are refused
8, sequencesa the sequence, 0 to 7; b 0 running, 1 passes completed since its start, 2 position in ticks within the pass, 3 waiting (1 while a start waits for its start tick)

A receiver reads a synthesizer's program, notes, velocities, fields, controllers and bend from the family's tracker it keeps for the sound, approximate by the stream's buffer for a sound whose blocks the server sends; it meters level, and a local sound's envelope and voices, only for the values some condition or command of the table names, at most MAX_WATCHED of them, and tells the meter nothing of any rule.

6.6 Groups and commands: the only thing a rule can run

DOC-6588 · reference · normative · NeoTeletext's own: no standard defines it · requirements REQ-6526, REQ-6612, REQ-6767

A table MAY hold 0 to MAX_GROUPS groups, numbered from 0 in the order written. A group is a list of 1 to MAX_GROUP_COMMANDS commands. Each command is one record's type and body, exactly the bytes the server would send that record with directly, at most MAX_COMMAND_BYTES of body, with up to MAX_COMMAND_BINDINGS bindings after it (amounts). A group is referenced by its number: by a rule, by a sequence's step and by a RUN command. To run a group is to apply its commands in written order, each exactly as the same record sent by the server is applied, with its amounts resolved first and its effect taken at once; a RUN command in a group runs the group it names in place, at that point. A command whose target, sound, group, timer or sequence does nothing useful when it runs (an object that does not exist, an audio channel with no sound) does nothing, is counted, and never stops the run. A run happens only in a handling (handlings).

A command in a group MUST be a record of one of these types, and its body's page field (and sub-code field, where the record has one) MUST be the table's own page:

TypeRecordIn a group it
3CONTROL, the audio profile'splays a sound the page already has, or stops or changes the gain of an audio channel. Its sequence field MUST be 0 and is not read; its page field MUST be the table's page number, so a group cannot start a sound for the whole service; its flags MUST NOT include "after the current sound"
15DRAWING_LINKSreplaces the links of the page's picture: a program's regis_links or naplps_links. Only one whole sending, part 0 of 1, within MAX_COMMAND_BYTES; a longer set of links is the server's to send directly
16REGIS_CURSORmakes a drawing or object the page's picture's cursor, or none: a program's regis_cursor or naplps_cursor
23ANIMATEchanges the animation state of the page's controls and objects: show, hide, look, move, order, frame, cycle, stop a cycle, reset (the animation state)
24SPRITESreplaces the page's teletext sprites
25NAPLPS_OBJECTSreplaces the page's NAPLPS objects
28LOCAL_MIDIgives one MIDI message to a local sound
29VARIABLEchanges a variable
30TIMERstarts or stops a timer
31REPORTreports to the page's channel
32RUNruns another group now
33SEQUENCEstarts or stops a sequence (sequences)

The six records of types 28 to 33 are the six command records. A picture's links and cursor may change at local speed because a receiver follows a picture's link itself under every rule of a link it follows: the destination shown while the pointer is on the target, the dwell time, and the question before leaving the channel. A group that changes them changes what the viewer is shown before anything is followed, never where a press already made goes. Every other record type MUST be refused in a group, and the table with it: a RULES record, and with it any definition of a group, a sequence, a row or a rectangle (a page cannot rewrite its own rules when triggered: what a table can do is fixed when it is checked); page content (REGIS, NAPLPS, SHEET and teletext packets, which are a stream the server owns and which a group's command limit could not hold); a sound's definition and its blocks (OBJECT, DATA); FRAME (a run is already applied whole and drawn in one frame); links and navigation (LINKS, SUBPAGES, REDIRECT, DENIED, INDEX, LOG), which must not change at local speed or move the viewer by a timer; and the session's records (CURSOR, INPUT_CONTROL, STATE_CHALLENGE, STATE_END, STATE_KEEP_OFFER, RULES_QUERY).
