11.13 Other files a receiver may read

DOC-1872 · reference · normative · requirements REQ-169, REQ-170, REQ-171, REQ-172, REQ-173, REQ-179, REQ-180

Unfinished. The project's records do not show all of this as met, so it may not hold in full: REQ-169 Format detection (to be rechecked on livedevelopment); REQ-170 MPEG transport stream packet sizes (to be rechecked on livedevelopment); REQ-171 Finding teletext streams in a transport stream (to be rechecked on livedevelopment); REQ-172 Teletext in elementary stream packets (to be rechecked on livedevelopment); REQ-173 Raw elementary stream files (to be rechecked on livedevelopment); REQ-179 Reader accepts EP1 page files (to be rechecked on livedevelopment); REQ-180 Reader accepts edit.tf and zxnet page addresses (to be rechecked on livedevelopment).

These are not files of a channel. A receiver that opens a file by itself decides its format by its content, and an explicit format overrides that. Page files begin with commands such as PN, or DE,, transport streams have 0x47 every 188, 192 or 204 bytes, elementary streams begin 00 00 01 BD, and EP1 files FE 01. For a headerless stream, a decoder tries each packet length and bit order and takes the one in which addresses decode best.

EP1 is a 6-byte header, an optional enhancement block when the flag is 0xCA, 25 rows of 40 bytes, and a 2-byte terminator. A file without enhancements is 1,008 bytes.

Transport streams. A reader accepts 188, 192 and 204-byte packets, regains synchronisation after corruption, and discards packets with the transport-error flag. It accepts packets with both an adaptation field and payload, though clause 4.1 permits only one. It finds teletext from the Program Map Table by stream type 0x06 with a teletext descriptor, and reports each entry. In an elementary stream packet with stream identifier 0xBD it accepts data identifiers 0x10 to 0x1F and 0x99 to 0x9B, reads data units 0x02, 0x03 and 0xC0, checks the framing code, and bit-reverses each of the 42 bytes. Other data units are skipped by their length.

edit.tf and zxnet addresses. A page may arrive in an address, as a metadata digit, a colon, and base64url of 25 rows of seven-bit codes.

Defined by: EN 300 472 V1.3.1 clause 4.1 Transport Stream (TS) packet format; EN 300 472 V1.3.1 clause 4.2 PES packet format; EN 300 472 V1.3.1 clause 4.3 Syntax for PES data field; EN 300 472 V1.3.1 clause 4.4 Semantics for PES data field; EN 300 472 V1.3.1 table 2 Syntax for Data_field for EBU Teletext; EN 300 472 V1.3.1 table 3 data_identifier; EN 300 472 V1.3.1 table 4 data_unit_id

11.14 Hand-written and built channels, and what is not built of them

DOC-2034 · reference · informative · NeoTeletext's own: no standard defines it · requirements REQ-1886, REQ-1893, REQ-1896, REQ-1903, REQ-1904

Unfinished. The project's records do not show all of this as met, so it may not hold in full: REQ-1886 Finding a page (tested, not recorded as met on main); REQ-1893 The bundle MUST NOT exceed 262,144 bytes (to be rechecked on main); REQ-1896 Derived files (tested, not recorded as met on main); REQ-1903 Media types of a channel's files (tested, not recorded as met on main); REQ-1904 Bounded readers: refuse oversize files (tested, not recorded as met on main).

Not built. M.pag, NNN.ep1 in a channel, and the build tool. This item gives the structure of a channel decided on 30 October 2026 in full, and the rest of it is built: page folders and sub-page files and a page's list say how. The structure decided and not built says what is left.

Principles. One structure is used unchanged by files on disk, an SD card, a file:// folder, any static host and the server. Every file a reader asks for is named from a page number, a sub-code or a part number. Every file has a maximum a microcontroller can hold, and no file grows with the size of the channel but the magazine lists, which the standard's page count bounds. What can be derived is generated, never written by hand: a list says what its files hold, and the file is the truth.

The files of the structure, where P is a part number in decimal, 0 to 127, with no leading zeros, and M a magazine, 1 to 8:

NameHoldsLargestTier
channel.ttxThe channel's settings16,384 bytesOptional
contents.txtThe table of contents65,536 bytes, 1,000 linesOptional
index.t42The first sub-page of any number of pages, so a channel opens with one request262,144 bytesBuilt
M.pagMagazine M's pages17,204 bytesBuilt
NNN.ttiPage NNN, with all its sub-pages262,144 bytesHand-written
NNN.t42Page NNN: all its sub-pages, or only the first when the page has a folder; then, optionally, one sub-page's picture records262,144 bytes of teletext packets; 2,224,090 bytes with a picture's recordsEither
NNN.ep1Page NNN, one sub-page: a 6-byte header, sixteen 40-byte enhancement packets, 25 rows of 40 bytes and a 2-byte terminator1,648 bytesHand-written
NNN/SSSS.t42Sub-page SSSS of page NNN; then, optionally, its picture records3,108 bytes of teletext packets; 1,965,054 bytes with a picture's recordsBuilt
NNN/SSSS.ttiSub-page SSSS of page NNN, as TTI262,144 bytesHand-written
NNN/P.subPart P of page NNN's list of sub-pages4,119 bytesBuilt
pushThe live connectionOne message 65,536 bytesOptional

A reader asks for these names and no others, and every name fits the 8.3 form a minimal FAT library reads. Every reader of one of these files refuses whole a file larger than its largest, and allocates no more than that bound. M.pag and NNN/P.sub are accepted as text/plain or application/octet-stream, NNN.ep1 as application/octet-stream, NNN/SSSS.t42 as NNN.t42 is, and NNN/SSSS.tti as NNN.tti is.

Pictures in T42 files. A sub-page's picture (renderer parity PAR-8: its ReGIS or NAPLPS stream, its NAPLPS objects, its drawing links and its cursor) is carried as record packets 4/31 on data channel 12 after the sub-page's teletext packets, in the sub-page's own file, and also in NNN.t42 when that sub-page is the page's first. A reader counts the teletext packets apart from the record packets: the teletext packets are bounded as the table's first figure says, and the whole file, with one picture's records, as its second. The second figure is the first plus the most one picture's records take, 1,961,946 bytes: a stream of 1,048,576 bytes in 129 records of at most 241 packets, one objects record of at most 199 packets, the drawing links in at most 64 records of at most 241 packets, and one cursor record of one packet, 46,713 packets of 42 bytes. A reader that cannot hold a file that large refuses it whole. index.t42 carries no pictures.

Hand-written. A folder with page files, NNN.tti, NNN.t42 or NNN.ep1, each holding the whole page, and optionally channel.ttx and contents.txt. Nothing else is needed, and a reader MUST open such a folder fully: it learns a page's sub-pages from the page's file as it decodes it. EP1 and edit.tf files carry no trusted page number, and in a channel the file's name gives it.

Built. What a generator writes, from a hand-written folder or from a program's pages: every page as NNN.t42, and a page of more than one sub-page with its folder NNN/ holding every sub-page's file and the parts of its list; the magazine lists; and index.t42. A built channel MAY also carry the hand-written files. Nobody writes a validator, a part or a magazine list by hand: a generator derives them from the page data, every time it writes them. A generator puts first sub-pages in index.t42 in ascending page order, and stops before the page that would pass the bound.

The build tool. neottx turns any folder into a built channel: a vbit2 service folder, captures, editor exports, files of any name with the page number read from each TTI's PN line or each EP1's name.

Finding a page. A reader looks in its store, when the page is there and confirmed current; then in NNN.tti, NNN.t42 and NNN.ep1, stopping at the first that answers 200 and passes its format's check; otherwise the page is not found, at a cost of at most three requests. Within a channel the extension that last answered 200 is tried first. A file that answers 200 and fails its check is a failure of that page, and the others are not tried.

11.15 Validators, versions and sub-page titles, and what is not built of them

DOC-2035 · reference · informative · NeoTeletext's own: no standard defines it · requirements REQ-1889, REQ-1891, REQ-1896

Unfinished. The project's records do not show all of this as met, so it may not hold in full: REQ-1891 Sub-page title (not implemented on main); REQ-1896 Derived files (tested, not recorded as met on main).

Not built. A built file's ETag, and a title taken from row 1 or carried in M.pag. A file's validator, a page's version and a list derived from its pages are built, and every part of a page's list carries them.

  • A file's validator is the first 16 lowercase hexadecimal digits of the SHA-256 of the file's bytes, as the engine's Validator::of writes it.
  • A page's version is the validator of the page's sub-pages' packets end to end, in the page's order: what NNN.t42 would hold if it held them all. It changes when any sub-page changes, is added or is removed.
  • A built file's ETag MUST be its validator in double quotes, so that a sub-page's validator in its list and the ETag of its file are one value. A reader that holds a sub-page compares the list's validator with the ETag it holds, and fetches only what differs, with no conditional request for the rest. A generator that cannot set headers, on a static host, gives up only that saving: the host's own ETag still serves conditional requests.
  • A generator derives every part, magazine list, validator, version and title from the page data each time it writes them. A reader treats a sub-page's file as the truth when it disagrees with a list.

A sub-page's title is, in this order:

  1. the title its publisher gave it: a program's sub-page title, or a TTI page's DE line for its first sub-page;
  2. otherwise the text of its row 1: each character shown in an alphanumeric mode whose code is 0x20 to 0x7E is kept as that ASCII character, and everything else, spacing attributes and mosaic characters included, becomes a space. Runs of spaces become one, the ends are trimmed, and the result is cut to 40 characters;
  3. otherwise, when that leaves nothing, it has none, and a list shows its sub-code and place alone.

Row 0 is never used: its text is the service's header, the same on every sub-page. A page's title, in M.pag, is its first sub-page's.

11.16 Decided, not built: magazine lists

DOC-2039 · reference · informative · NeoTeletext's own: no standard defines it · requirements REQ-1892

Unfinished. The project's records do not show all of this as met, so it may not hold in full: REQ-1892 Magazine lists (not implemented on main).

Not built. Nothing reads or writes M.pag.

M.pag lists magazine M's pages, so that a reader knows which pages exist, how many sub-pages each has, whether it changed and what it is called, without asking for any page. It says what the standard's Magazine Inventory Page says, with the exact counts the inventory gives only as ranges above 79, and titles.

The format is text, as a list of sub-pages is, with no header: the number of lines is the number of pages. Every line is one page, in ascending page number:

FieldHolds
pageNNN, a page of magazine M: any page number but the reserved ones, MFD, MFE and MFF in every magazine, and 1BE and 1F0
sub-pagesIts number of sub-pages in decimal, 1 to 8,190
versionThe page's version
titleOptional: 1 to 40 characters, its first sub-page's title

Size. A magazine has at most 253 pages, a line is at most 3 + 1 + 4 + 1 + 16 + 1 + 40 + 2 = 68 bytes, and a magazine list is at most 253 × 68 = 17,204 bytes. All eight are at most 137,632 bytes, and a reader needs only the magazine being browsed.

Faults. A line of another magazine's page, a reserved page, a page not above the line before it, or an invalid field is ignored and counted. A magazine list that answers 404 or 410 means the channel does not list that magazine, not that it is empty: a reader then finds its pages by asking for them.

With contents.txt. contents.txt is the channel's own table of contents, in the order and sections it chooses, of at most 800 keyable pages. The magazine lists are the inventory of every page, hexadecimal ones included. A reader shows the first and navigates by the second.

11.17 Decided, not built: opening any address

DOC-2036 · reference · informative · NeoTeletext's own: no standard defines it · requirements REQ-1898, REQ-1899, REQ-1900

Unfinished. The project's records do not show all of this as met, so it may not hold in full: REQ-1898 Any address is opened in the order of DOC-2036, and one that fits none is refused with a reason (tested, not recorded as met on main); REQ-1899 Single resource read as DOC-2036 says (not implemented on main); REQ-1900 A folder on this computer opens as a channel (not implemented on main).

Not built. What a receiver does today is in opening a channel and other files a receiver may read. The order below, the bound of a single resource and a folder on this computer as a channel by this structure are decided and not built.

A reader opens any address it is given. It decides what the address is in this order, and stops at the first that fits.

#The addressOpens as
1Its fragment is a page in the edit.tf or zxnet editors' form, a hexadecimal digit, a colon and the base64url page. Never on an http or https address, where a fragment is refusedThat page alone, decoded from the address, with nothing fetched
2A folder: its path ends in /A channel
3A channel's folder followed by one of the fixed names of the structureThat channel, at the page or sub-page the name gives: a page's or sub-page's file name is normalised to its place in the URL map. A receiver's file that names no page, such as index.t42, is refused as a viewer's address, and a program told to open one opens its channel
4Any other address that answers 200 with teletextA single resource, in every reader but the browser
5Any other address that answers 200 with a web pageIn every reader but the browser, discovery: its Link headers and <link> elements lead to a channel
6A live feed in the zxnet viewer's WebSocket formThat live stream
7Anything elseRefused, saying why

In the browser every http and https address must be an address of the URL map when it is read, so what would be case 4 or 5 falls to case 7, refused with a sentence for the viewer, with no tab opened and no fetcher started. The address field alone adds a channel's missing final slash first. The security rules apply to every case, whatever it opens as: the plain-HTTP mark, no downgrade, the local-network checks, strict HTTP, and the rules of redirects.

A single resource is a file that is not part of a channel, with any name, anywhere.

  • Its format is decided by its content, never by its name or extension: a T42 recording, a transport stream, sliced VBI data, a TTI file or an EP1 file. Of these the browser reads T42 and TTI alone, and neottx and the engine's readers keep the others. It holds whatever pages, sub-pages and enhancements it holds.
  • Its identity is its own address, not a folder. It has no settings, no lists, no live connection and no cookies. Its links lead only to pages it holds, and any other link is a navigation away from it, shown as one.
  • It is read whole, at most MAX_SINGLE_RESOURCE, 64 MiB, in the process that reads network data, and played to the decoder as a local file is.
  • It is never interactive. Taking the viewer's keys needs a channel.

Folders and files on this computer. A folder on this computer is a channel by the same structure, with the same names and rules, and a folder that holds no file of the structure opens as an empty channel at its initial page, which is not found. A file on this computer is a single resource, whatever its name. In the browser a file is its own channel with no cookies, read as T42 or TTI alone, any other format being refused, and it is loaded at once. A file: address takes the places of the URL map after #, the one use of #.

11.18 Decided, not built: presentation

DOC-2037 · reference · informative · NeoTeletext's own: no standard defines it · requirements REQ-1901, REQ-1902

Unfinished. The project's records do not show all of this as met, so it may not hold in full: REQ-1901 A channel whose presentation is "site" switches off page numbers, magazines, pages and sub-pages for its viewers, and no viewer can switch them back on (not implemented on main); REQ-1902 A channel cannot alter the reader's trusted indicators and controls; a "site" channel's address shows the channel without its page (not implemented on main).

Not built. channel.ttx has no member presentation today, and one is refused as unknown.

A member presentation of channel.ttx, "teletext" or "site", by default "teletext", says how a reader shows the channel. It changes nothing about the structure.

  • "teletext": the reader's whole interface: the overview of the channel's pages, the contents, the list and count of a page's sub-pages, and keying page numbers.
  • "site": the channel is shown as a site of linked pages. By default the reader hides the overview, the contents, and the list and count of sub-pages, and keying digits does not select a page: they go to the channel when it takes keys, and do nothing otherwise. The viewer moves only by what the pages offer: their links, their Fastext keys, the prompts they make clickable, and back and forward through the pages they have seen. Every page keeps its address and can be bookmarked and shared.

It is one switch, not a member a panel, so that no channel can make a half of one and half of the other.

What presentation never changes. No member, file or page of a channel hides, moves or changes the reader's trusted indicators and controls: its strip and the address it shows, row 0 columns 0 to 7, which belong to the receiver alone, what says keys go to the channel, and the keys the reader keeps for itself. The viewer stays in charge: the reader's own menu still opens the overview and the sub-page list of a "site" channel.

Presentation is not secrecy. Every file is still at its fixed address, and index.t42 and the lists name every page to anyone who asks. A page only some viewers may see is sent by a program to those viewers, over the live connection.

11.19 Decided, not built: fetching a page's enhancement pages

DOC-2128 · reference · informative · NeoTeletext's own: no standard defines it · requirements REQ-511

Unfinished. The project's records do not show all of this as met, so it may not hold in full: REQ-511 Fetch enhancement dependencies once (to be rechecked on livedevelopment).

Not built. No reader does this. When a viewer shows a page of a channel at Level 2.5 or 3.5 and its enhancement pages are not in the store, it is to ask once for its magazine's Organization Table, page xFE, and then for the object pages the table and the page name. Pages already stored are not asked for again, and these requests do not change which page is kept current. While they load the page shows with what has arrived, and is drawn again as they arrive. A dependency that cannot be fetched removes only what depends on it.

12 The program protocol

DOC-1787 · section

12.1 A program behind a channel

DOC-1964 · concept · informative · NeoTeletext's own: no standard defines it · requirements REQ-1474, REQ-1476

Unfinished. The project's records do not show all of this as met, so it may not hold in full: REQ-1474 The server keeps no channel content beyond per-connection state, one last-sent sub-page per connection, and a short cache of public pages' descriptions (to be rechecked on livedevelopment); REQ-1476 The server and a program MUST exchange only the closed set of exactly typed messages, with no view field (to be rechecked on livedevelopment).

A channel's program runs outside the server, in any language, and one program serves every viewer of its channel, multiplexed by connection, one browser tab each. It never sees packets, unless it asks to send them raw, or connections' sockets, headers or the keys of viewer state: of a viewer it sees only each connection's viewer handle, when the viewer has given state. The server relays: a program owns every page, and the server holds only what each open connection is, and the last sub-page it sent it, and for a minute what a page shows the web.

The conversation is one JSON object a line, in both directions. A viewer's selection reaches the program as a request that stays open: the server sends selected, the program answers with a sub-page, and may send that sub-page again at any time as it changes, until the viewer selects something else. A channel can differ for every viewer, because the program answers each connection as it chooses.

The kits for TypeScript and Python are conveniences over this protocol: it is the interface, and a program in any language can speak it directly.

12.2 Processes, transports and lines

DOC-1965 · reference · normative · NeoTeletext's own: no standard defines it · requirements REQ-1034, REQ-1042, REQ-1043, REQ-1044, REQ-1045, REQ-1056, REQ-1348, REQ-1475, REQ-1479, REQ-4120

Unfinished. The project's records do not show all of this as met, so it may not hold in full: REQ-1034 A program started again is told of its viewers (to be rechecked on livedevelopment); REQ-1042 Standard input and output (to be rechecked on livedevelopment); REQ-1043 A Unix domain socket, for a program that runs as a service of its own (to be rechecked on livedevelopment); REQ-1045 One protocol on every transport (to be rechecked on livedevelopment); REQ-1056 `start` ends every connection a program knew (to be rechecked on livedevelopment); REQ-1348 A channel flushes each line it writes to the server (to be rechecked on main); REQ-1475 Every message between server and program has one exact typed shape and a faulty message is refused whole (to be rechecked on livedevelopment); REQ-1479 Protocol messages are JSON lines, one per line, ended by a line feed (to be rechecked on livedevelopment).

The protocol's version is 16. Three transports carry the same lines.

  • Standard input and output. The server starts each channel's program as the channels file says, in its own folder, with NEOTELETEXT_CHANNEL set to the channel's folder. A program's standard error becomes the server's log, a line an event, cut at 64 KiB.
  • A Unix domain socket. A channel named with a socket is served to the program that connects to it, which runs as a service of its own and so outlives a restart of the server. The socket and its folder are their owner's alone. One program at a time. When it goes, or the server restarts, it connects again and is sent start again.
  • A WebSocket, for a program on another machine. A channel named with a secret_variable or a secret_file is served to the program that opens a WebSocket to /<channel>/program with Authorization: Bearer and the channel's secret, as the server's part describes. Each WebSocket message carries the same lines. Without exactly that secret the answer is 401; while a program is connected another is answered 409. One program at a time, served as one on a socket is. A program without a WebSocket of its own reaches it through the bridge, scripts/bridge.ts of neoteletext-app-server.

Lines. One JSON object a line (RFC 8259), UTF-8, ending in a line feed, at most 16 MiB. A program MUST flush each line as it writes it. Every message is an object tagged by type. Every line a program sends is checked whole and refused whole when it is not valid: the program is sent refused, and nothing of the line is acted on. An unknown type or field is refused, never skipped, and so is a field given twice.

The exact contract is a JSON Schema, draft 2020-12, generated from the server's types and published as protocol/schema-16.json of neoteletext-app-server: its $defs/ServerMessage is what the server sends, and its $defs/ProgramMessage what a program sends. The schema holds every bound; this part says what each message is for.

Starting and ending. When a program starts or connects, the server sends it start, then connected for every connection open. start ends every connection the program knew: it forgets each, and all it holds for it, since it will hear nothing more of a connection the server no longer has, and a connection the server still has comes back with connected as a new one. What it keeps under a viewer's handle in a store of its own outlasts start. While no program runs, a channel has nothing to show, and each selection ends with DENIED 503. A program that ends is started again after 1 second, then 2, 4 and so on up to 30. One that ran 5 seconds or more was ended, not failing, and is started again at once.

Queues. The network loop never waits for a program. At most 4,096 lines wait for it, and beyond that the newest are dropped and the server's log says so. A pointer's move takes none of that room: each connection has one move waiting, which a newer one replaces until the program takes it, at most 60 a second (the pointer's moves). Lines for a program that is not running are dropped, since it is told of every viewer when it starts. Timers are a program's own: it has a clock.

The channels file is a JSON object with one member, channels, a list of objects. Each has a folder of letters, digits, - and _, a name, and one of: a command, a list, and a directory, taken from the file's own folder when relative; a socket; or a secret_variable (an environment variable of the server's) or secret_file (a file, at most 4,096 bytes, taken from the file's own folder when relative) naming where the program's secret is, never the secret itself. initial_page, three decimal digits, is the channel's initial page, 100 when left out. default_rules, "none" (the default) or "send_all", is what a page has when its program gave it no rule table (the default table), and wheel, true or false, adds the wheel to the default table:

{"channels":[{"folder":"example","name":"Example","command":["python3","program.py"],"directory":"example","default_rules":"none"}]}

12.3 Common shapes

DOC-1966 · reference · normative · NeoTeletext's own: no standard defines it · requirements REQ-1471, REQ-1475, REQ-1476, REQ-1502

Unfinished. The project's records do not show all of this as met, so it may not hold in full: REQ-1471 The server holds a viewer's connection event for the first SELECT and sends the program one connected event (to be rechecked on livedevelopment); REQ-1475 Every message between server and program has one exact typed shape and a faulty message is refused whole (to be rechecked on livedevelopment); REQ-1476 The server and a program MUST exchange only the closed set of exactly typed messages, with no view field (to be rechecked on livedevelopment); REQ-1502 Each live connection has exactly one selection, made of one page number and one sub-code (to be rechecked on main).

ShapeMeaning
connectionA whole number from 1, below 253, naming one open connection: one tab, with one selection, from its opening until gone. Never reused while the server runs.
viewerA viewer's handle on this channel: 32 lower-case hexadecimal digits, the same on every connection of that viewer to this channel and meaningless outside it, or null while the connection has no viewer. A program may use it only to provide what the viewer asked for on this channel
pageThree hexadecimal digits in capitals, the magazine 1 to 8 first, "100" to "8FF"
subFour, "0000" to "3F7F", with no bit outside the thirteen, where "3F7F" means the page and none of its sub-pages in particular
requestA whole number from 1: the number of a connection's selection
connections"all", every open connection, or a list of 1 to 4,096 connections. A connection named that has closed is passed over.
Text, in every fieldUTF-8 in Unicode normalisation form C, with no control character and no bidirectional formatting character, within the field's length
BytesExact base64 (RFC 4648 section 4), padded, with no white space

A connection's selection is a page with sub"3F7F", answered with the page's first sub-page in ascending sub-code order, which then becomes the selection; or one sub-page. A sub-page never changes by itself.

12.4 The request number

DOC-1967 · reference · normative · NeoTeletext's own: no standard defines it · requirements REQ-1473, REQ-1481

Unfinished. The project's records do not show all of this as met, so it may not hold in full: REQ-1481 A selection the program does not answer in time ends with DENIED 503 and the connection stays open (to be rechecked on livedevelopment).

The server gives each selection on a connection a rising number, from 1, and passes it to the program in connected and selected. The program's reply, page, subpages, redirect and denied for that selection carry it back as request. The server drops any whose number is not the connection's current selection, and counts it as stale_answers. So a late answer cannot replace the page now on screen, and a program that was slow did nothing wrong: it is not refused.

This is between the server and a program. The viewer's input protocol does not carry it.

  • reply, redirect and denied MUST carry a number. page and subpages may carry null, which says it is a change.
  • A reply to a selection already replaced still gives the index, since that is the connection's, and its sub-page is dropped.
  • A number belongs to one connection, so a page or subpages that carries one names exactly one, and one that names others is refused with the rule one_connection.
  • A page with a request of null is a change: it reaches connections whose selection it shows, and that have had their answer. A connection still awaiting its answer is not sent it, since that answer will be current.
  • A redirect for a selection already replaced is dropped: the viewer's own choice overrides it. A redirect to a page is itself a new selection, with a new number.

The ending.denied ends a selection at once. A reply whose selected is null does not end one: it says only that the page goes separately, and a page, redirect or denied must follow, or the deadline does. A redirect to another channel ends one.

12.5 From the server to a program

DOC-1968 · reference · normative · NeoTeletext's own: no standard defines it · requirements REQ-1033, REQ-1053, REQ-1056, REQ-1471, REQ-1472, REQ-1476, REQ-2215, REQ-6532, REQ-6733, REQ-6766, REQ-6767, REQ-6900

Unfinished. The project's records do not show all of this as met, so it may not hold in full: REQ-1053 Server figures are measured (to be rechecked on livedevelopment); REQ-1056 `start` ends every connection a program knew (to be rechecked on livedevelopment); REQ-1471 The server holds a viewer's connection event for the first SELECT and sends the program one connected event (to be rechecked on livedevelopment); REQ-1472 A connection's selection comes only from SELECT, and the server forwards only the selected sub-page (to be rechecked on livedevelopment); REQ-1476 The server and a program MUST exchange only the closed set of exactly typed messages, with no view field (to be rechecked on livedevelopment); REQ-2215 Server's start message carries the closed list of languages (to be rechecked on livedevelopment); REQ-6733 What a program is told of viewer state: connected carries viewer and remembered, and viewer_began, viewer_left, state_refused, viewers_reset and gone (not implemented on livedevelopment); REQ-6900 Program protocol 16 carries snapshots: the server's snapshot message names no connection or viewer, and a program answers only with snapshot_page or snapshot_declined (tested, not recorded as met on livedevelopment).

typeFieldsWhen
startprotocol (16), epoch_ms, standard, budgets, languagesThe program started or connected. It ends every connection the program knew: forget each, and all you hold for it. connected follows for each connection open, as a new one.
connectedconnection, request; selection, page and sub, or null for the channel's initial page; path, that selection as an address names it, or null; query, the query of the address selected, as written, or null; viewer, the viewer's handle on this channel, 32 characters 0 to 9 and a to f, or null; remembered, whether the viewer chose to be remembered on this channel, false when viewer is nullA connection, one browser tab, opened and its first selection came, or 1.5 seconds passed with none. Answer with reply.
selectedconnection, request, path, 302 or 302/0002, page, sub, queryThe connection selected a page, sub 3F7F, so send its first sub-page and its subpages list; or one sub-page, so send that. Every selection is a new one for the page's rule table and animation: send the page's table, sheets, definitions and object pages with it, since the server keeps none. A picture sent to the audience "kept" is the one thing the server sends a selection itself (kept pictures).
inputconnection, page, sub, lost, rule, row, tick, target, eventInput on the page on screen that a rule of the page's rule table reported. page and sub are what the viewer was looking at, the connection's selection, except that a release names the page that held it. lost is true on a release the page lost. rule is the name of the rule that reported it, row the place of the firing row in the rule's row set or null, tick the page tick it belongs to, and target the target the pointer was inside, or null.
rule_eventconnection, page, sub, rule, row, tick, event: {"kind":"fired"}, or {"kind":"value","read":…,"value":n}A REPORT of the page's table reported a firing with no input event (a timer, a sequence, a cue, open, close, becomes, a command the server sent), or one value. rule is null when no rule made the run. See the rule table's messages.
page_stateconnection, page, sub, request, tick, table, variables, timers, sequences, targets, valuesThe answer to query_state: one page's local state in one viewer's receiver, once
rules_faultconnection, page, sub, generation, fault, countA receiver reported a fault of the page's table, at most once a second for each fault and page

viewer_beganconnection, viewer, rememberedA connection that had no viewer now has one: after request_state, or when the viewer offered state

viewers_resetNoneEvery viewer handle the program knows is void

refusedmessage, its type or null; path of the first fault, such as page.rows[3], page.text[2] or parts[3].text; rule; detail, in words; request, the request number of the message refused when it carried one (a reply, page, subpages, redirect, denied, measure, measure_picture_text or query_state), else null; sound, the sound a refused sound message concerns by its kind, handle and generation, else nullA line the program sent was refused whole, and nothing of it was done
describepage, and nothing else: no connection, viewer or queryA web visitor or a search engine is at the page's address, or the program has just started: the server asks once then, for page 100 and with no visitor, and any answer makes the channel ready. Answer with description, built from no viewer: nothing says who asked, and the answer goes to everyone for up to a minute. See describing a page.

Answer within snapshot_limit_ms with snapshot_page or snapshot_declined, drawn for no one in particular: the answer may go to any stranger for up to a minute. See snapshots, for a program.
measuredrequest, the number measure gave; triplets; limit, 208; designation; runsThe answer to measure: what the page's encoding costs, the page sent to no viewer. See measuring a page.
measured_picture_textrequest, the number measure_picture_text gave; cells; regis_bytes; naplps_bytes; sets; stand_insThe answer to measure_picture_text: what a text part costs in a picture, sent to no viewer. See text in pictures.

A stored synthesizer sound also brings sound_built, with what reading it dropped (the sound message). There is no session that spans connections and no cookie: a viewer known across tabs is the viewer handle, which a program may use only to provide what the viewer asked for on this channel.

The version. protocol is the protocol's one version, a whole number. It is raised by one on every change to the shape or meaning of any message, in either direction, and there is no compatibility path and no range of versions. A program MUST stop on a start of a version other than the one it was built for. Version 16 differs from 15 in meaning: every place, size and move of a NAPLPS object, every rectangle and pointer place of a rule table on a NAPLPS page, and where a NAPLPS picture is drawn are dots of the 480 by 500 teletext raster, the picture drawn on lines 20 to 479 (NAPLPS objects), where 15 used a picture of 640 by 480; a program built for 15 would put every object in the wrong place without an error. The picture messages are part of 16 as they are described there. Snapshots, snapshot, snapshot_page, snapshot_declined and snapshot_limit_ms, were added to 16 before it was released, without a new version.

standard is the standard's maxima, so that a program holds none of its own: magazines 8, pages 2,022, pages_per_magazine 253, pages_in_magazine_1 251, keyable_pages 800, subpages 8,190, decimal_subpages 3,199, numbered_subpages, the sub-pages automatic numbering can number, and link_target_bytes, the longest link target in bytes.

budgets is the server's own: line_bytes, 16 MiB; title_characters, 120; author_log_bytes, 200; log_characters, 1,000; named_connections, 4,096; reply_limit_ms, how long the server waits for an answer to connected or selected; description_text_characters, 16,000; description_limit_ms, how long a web visitor waits for a description; snapshot_limit_ms, 2,000, how long the server waits for an answer to snapshot.

languages is the closed list of the languages a page or a run of text may name: the engine's table of languages, in its order, fixed when the server is built and not configurable. Each entry has exactly a tag, the BCP 47 tag a page or run names it by, such as ru, sr-Latn or ja-Kana; a name, in English; and a direction, ltr or rtl. A tag not in the list is refused with the rule unknown_language. How text in these languages is written is text in any language.

rule is one of syntax, line_too_long, unknown_field, missing_field, duplicate_field, wrong_type, not_listed, out_of_range, too_long, too_short, not_ascending, duplicate, reserved, wrong_magazine, forbidden_character, not_nfc, not_base64, wrong_length, not_in_index, unknown_connection, not_awaited, outside_profile, invalid_packet, one_connection, wrong_page; the rules of pictures: invalid_regis, invalid_drawing_links, invalid_naplps, invalid_naplps_links, invalid_picture_parts, kept_over_limit, wrong_picture_language and not_kept; the rules of viewer state: has_viewer, no_gesture and unknown_viewer; the rules of text: language_and_character_set, unknown_language, text_cell_taken, text_set_changed, triplets_over_budget, text_unshown, text_overlap, text_out_of_columns and text_and_objects; the rules of the sound message (the sound message); the rules of the rule table's messages: rules_over_limit, invalid_rules, invalid_group, invalid_command, unknown_name, duplicate_name, unknown_parameter, too_frequent and not_answered; and the rules of animation's messages: frame_order, frame_too_large, invalid_animation, invalid_sprites, invalid_naplps_objects, invalid_sheet, sheet_too_large, too_many_timelines and invalid_object_page.

stats holds in server: uptime_s, connections, connections_peak, connections_total, messages_sent, bytes_sent, requests, restarts, memory_kb, channels, and viewers by channel folder. In channel it holds viewers, viewers_peak, viewers_total, opens, most_opened (at most ten), inputs, keys, pages_sent, subpages_not_forwarded, refused, invalid_packets, stale_input, stale_answers, redirects, sound_records, lines_to_application, lines_from_application, lines_dropped, proofs_accepted and proofs_refused. Each of the two also carries all_time. Nothing in it identifies a viewer, and no snapshot connection is counted in it.

Rests on: EN 300 706 V1.2.1 clause 9.6.1 Packets X/27/0 to X/27/3 for Editorial Linking

12.6 Snapshots, for a program

DOC-6904 · reference · normative · NeoTeletext's own: no standard defines it · requirements REQ-6900, REQ-6901, REQ-6902, REQ-6903

Unfinished. The project's records do not show all of this as met, so it may not hold in full: REQ-6900 Program protocol 16 carries snapshots: the server's snapshot message names no connection or viewer, and a program answers only with snapshot_page or snapshot_declined (tested, not recorded as met on livedevelopment); REQ-6901 The TypeScript kit answers a snapshot by running the page's selection for a stranger on a snapshot connection of its own, sending only the page and its picture (tested, not recorded as met on livedevelopment); REQ-6902 The Python kit answers a snapshot by running the page's selection for a stranger on a snapshot connection of its own, sending only the page and its picture (tested, not recorded as met on livedevelopment); REQ-6903 The component library draws a page for a snapshot connection as for a stranger: no kept viewer state, no parameters, no effects beyond drawing, and a page may opt out (tested, not recorded as met on livedevelopment).

A receiver may ask a channel for a picture of one page as a stranger who has just arrived would see it, on a snapshot connection. The server asks the channel's program to draw it with snapshot, a message that names no connection and no viewer, and the program answers with one sub-page and its picture, or declines. Nothing else can be sent to a snapshot: its number is not a connection, so no other message can name it.

Direction and typeFieldsMeaning
Server to program: snapshotsnapshot, its number, from 1, never reused while the server runs and counted apart from connections; page; sub, or 3F7F for the page as a whole; path, 302 or 302/0002; and nothing else: no connection, viewer, remembered, query or requestDraw this page for no one in particular, as for a connection that has just arrived with no viewer and no query. Answer within budgets.snapshot_limit_ms with snapshot_page or snapshot_declined.
Program to server: snapshot_pagesnapshot; page, one sub-page as a page message carries it, of the page asked for and of its sub-code, or of any sub-code when 3F7F was asked (a kit gives the first in ascending order); picture, optional: {"kept": sub} for the picture kept for that same sub-page, or {"language": "regis" | "naplps", "data": …} or with parts in place of data, with a NAPLPS picture's objects, at most 262,144 bytes decodedThe page as a stranger sees it. It is checked as every page and picture message is. It may be shown to any stranger for up to a minute.
Program to server: snapshot_declinedsnapshotThis page is not drawn for strangers. The server may then answer from the page's description when it is public.

An answer naming a snapshot the server does not await, answered already or late, is refused not_awaited. A snapshot_page of another page or sub-code is refused wrong_page, one naming a picture not kept not_kept, and one whose picture breaks a picture rule with that rule; each is then taken as declined. A message that names a snapshot's number as a connection is refused unknown_connection.

Draw a snapshot from nothing that belongs to one viewer. The request has no viewer, no query and no session, and the answer goes to everyone who asks within the minute. Decline a page that is not for strangers.

The NeoTeletext server asks at most 10 snapshots a second of a program, with a burst of 20, at most 16 unanswered at once, waits 2,000 ms for each, keeps each answer, a decline included, for 60 seconds for its page and sub-code, and asks two snapshot connections of one place once. When the page's public description is already at hand it answers from that and asks the program nothing. budgets.snapshot_limit_ms is 2,000.

What the kits do. Both kits answer snapshot themselves. They run the page's selection for a stranger on a connection of their own, numbered below zero and never sent to the server: the application is told the connection joined, asked for the page and opened it, as for a connection that has just arrived with no viewer and no query, and isSnapshot(connection) (Python is_snapshot) is true for it. The kit answers with the sub-page that connection would be shown first, and the picture sent to it alone or kept for that sub-page, then tells the application the connection left and is gone. Nothing else the application sends to it goes anywhere: no rules, sound, links, cursor, animation, sub-page list, index, author's log or viewer-state request, and messages to everyone or to a page's viewers never reach it. The kit declines when no application serves the page, the page's entry says snapshots: false (Python: the page is in no_snapshots), the application denies or redirects the connection, it has nothing to show, or a handler fails. The component library draws a snapshot's page with no viewer's kept state and no parameters, and runs no sound, stream or state request for it.

Snapshots were added to version 16 before 16 was released, without a new version.

12.7 What a program hears of input

DOC-1969 · reference · normative · NeoTeletext's own: no standard defines it · requirements REQ-207, REQ-1347, REQ-1367, REQ-1476, REQ-1557, REQ-6523, REQ-6532

Unfinished. The project's records do not show all of this as met, so it may not hold in full: REQ-207 Held input is released when the page loses keyboard focus (to be rechecked on livedevelopment); REQ-1347 The server passes a channel program the key modifiers, the mouse's dot and modifiers, and COMPOSE (to be rechecked on main); REQ-1476 The server and a program MUST exchange only the closed set of exactly typed messages, with no view field (to be rechecked on livedevelopment); REQ-1557 Server checks input page stamp against the connection's selection (to be rechecked on livedevelopment); REQ-6523 The browser sends the server no input event for a page unless the page's rule table asks for it (tested, not recorded as met on main).

A program is given an input only for an event that a rule of the page's rule table, fired by that event, reported with a REPORT of the firing in the event's own handling: a page with no table gives its program no input at all. On a channel whose server gives its pages the default table, that is every key, click, move and hover, and a program ignores what it does not use. Each input names, beside its event, the rule that reported it, the row (the place of the firing row in the rule's row set, or null), the page tick it belongs to, and the target the pointer was inside for a pointer trigger whose rule named a control, an object or a rectangle, else null. event.kind is one of these.

kindFields
keyaction, press, repeat or release; key, the name in the last column of the code table, or one character; mods; text and base, or null
mouseaction, press, release or move; button, 0 left, 1 middle, 2 right, null on a move; buttons, left, middle and right on a move, else null; mods; column, 0 to 39; row, 0 to 24; px and py
wheeldx, dy in 1/120ths of a line, down positive; mods; column, row; px and py
hoveraction, enter or leave; the control's first column and row
composetext, an input method's text as it stands, empty when composing ended; cursor, the caret in code points from its start
text, pastetext
focus, blurNone

mods is the modifier keys held, a whole number 0 to 255 with a bit each as KEY numbers them: 1 Shift, 2 Alt, 4 Control, 8 Super, 16 Hyper, 32 Meta, 64 Caps Lock, 128 Num Lock. Control-C is the key c with mods 4 and no text.

px and py are the dot of the page image under the pointer, 12 to a cell across and 20 down from the page's top left (where the pointer is), or null when the receiver does not know it. The dot always lies in the event's cell: the server drops an event whose dot does not.

A compose event carries no input of its own: what the input method commits comes as text. It is stamped, so one aimed at a page no longer selected is dropped.

Input stamped with anything but the connection's selection is dropped before it reaches a program, except a release. A report with no input event (a rule_event) is given whatever the connection has selected since, so that a close rule's report arrives. A program selects pages for a viewer with redirect.

A button above 2 is not passed on, and a wheel's delta is held to 16 bits.

A click is the left button's press: a mouse event with action press and button 0. The kits for Python and TypeScript and the UI component library click there, and nowhere else: their clicked is that press, and a component's click comes with it. A release, lost or not, is never a click.

A pointer's gone reaches a program as the release of each button the pointer held, marked lost, with mods 0 and no dot, since nothing pressed it. A lost release is no click, and a program MUST NOT act on it as on a release: the viewer did not let go, the pointer went. Both kits give a program the mark. A lost release is given only for a press that some rule reported, and names that press's rule, row and tick. A program hears no TOUCH event and no contact after the first, no RESIZE, and nothing of the device a pointer event came from.

12.8 From a program to the server

DOC-1970 · reference · normative · NeoTeletext's own: no standard defines it · requirements REQ-1473, REQ-1476, REQ-1477, REQ-1480, REQ-2216, REQ-6532, REQ-6533, REQ-6734, REQ-6735, REQ-6766, REQ-6767, REQ-6900

Unfinished. The project's records do not show all of this as met, so it may not hold in full: REQ-1476 The server and a program MUST exchange only the closed set of exactly typed messages, with no view field (to be rechecked on livedevelopment); REQ-1477 The server refuses, whole, a reply or index whose magazines and pages, or a reply whose selected sub-page, are not exactly shaped and bounded (to be rechecked on livedevelopment); REQ-1480 Every program message that reaches a viewer is sent as checked T42 packets (to be rechecked on livedevelopment); REQ-2216 When a program sends measure, the server answers without sending the page to any viewer (to be rechecked on livedevelopment); REQ-6734 What a program may ask of viewer state: request_state, end_state and offer_remember, and nothing else; the cookie message is removed (not implemented on livedevelopment); REQ-6735 The server refuses a program's viewer-state request the viewer has not given: has_viewer, no_gesture, unknown_viewer and the existing refusals (not implemented on livedevelopment); REQ-6900 Program protocol 16 carries snapshots: the server's snapshot message names no connection or viewer, and a program answers only with snapshot_page or snapshot_declined (tested, not recorded as met on livedevelopment).

typeFieldsWhat it does
replyconnection, request, magazines, selected, one sub-page or nullThe answer to connected, exactly once: the channel's index for this viewer, and the sub-page its selection shows, or the initial page's first. The page MUST be listed in magazines. A second one is refused with not_awaited.
pageconnections, request or null, page: one sub-pageIt reaches only those connections whose selection shows it: those that selected that page and sub-code. A selection of a page with 3F7F that is still waiting for its answer is ended only by the answer that carries its request, whose sub-page then becomes the selection; a page without that request is not forwarded to it. A sub-page sent to a connection the program named that does not show it is not forwarded and is counted in the channel's figure subpages_not_forwarded; one sent to every connection is not counted.
deniedconnection, request, status, 403, 404, 429 or 503Ends a selection with no page, at once. The viewer is sent DENIED, and the connection stays open.
subpagesconnections, request or null, page, version, 0 to 65,535, subpages: sub and title, at most 40 characters or null, each sub-code once, in ascending orderA page's list of sub-pages, with the answer to a page selection and whenever it changes. Sent to the connections named whose selection shows the page and that do not hold that version.
indexconnections, magazinesThe index changed
redirectconnection, request, and page and sub, with a query it keeps or none, or address, at most 8,000 bytesSends the viewer elsewhere, with no action from them. With a page, a selection, so the program is then sent selected for it. With an address, no selection changes, and the program is sent left when the viewer goes. Naming both or neither is refused.
soundkind, connections, and the kind's fieldsA sound, its data, or a command. A local sound is announced with one of the kinds that end _local.
regis, regis_links, regis_cursor, naplps, naplps_links, naplps_cursorconnections or "kept", page, sub, and each its own fields; regis and naplps take data or partsA sub-page's picture drawn in ReGIS or NAPLPS, the links of its drawings or objects, and its cursor, sent as their own records to the connections that agreed the language, and kept for later viewers with "kept": see picture messages, kept pictures and text in pictures
forget_picturepage, subDrops the kept picture of that page and sub-code; one with nothing kept is refused not_kept. See kept pictures.
measure_picture_textrequest, a number from 0 to 232 less one that the program chooses; text; language or null; outsideAsks what a text part costs in a picture. It reaches no viewer; the server answers measured_picture_text or refused: see text in pictures.
rulesconnections, page, sub, table, a rule table or nullGives a page its rule table, or removes it: see the rule table's messages. The table is what asks for the viewer's input on that page. The server keeps none: a program sends it at every selection of the page.
local_midi, variable, timer, report, run, sequenceconnections, page, sub, and each command's own fieldsThe commands a group of a rule table may hold, sent directly to the connections that have the page selected: a MIDI message to a local sound, a change of a variable, a timer started or stopped, a report of a value, a group run now, a sequence started or stopped. See the rule table's messages.
query_stateconnection, page, sub, request, 1 to 232 less oneAsks one connection for one page's local state, once. The server answers page_state or refused.
frame, animate, sprites, naplps_objects, sprite_sheet, timeline, timeline_stop, object_pageconnections, page, sub, and each its own fields; naplps_objects also takes "kept"Animation: an atomic frame's begin and end, operations on a page's objects, a teletext page's sprites, a NAPLPS page's objects, bytes of a page's sprite sheet, a timeline of operations the server plays and its stopping, and a teletext object page a page's sprites use: see animation's messages and the object_page message.
request_stateconnectionAsks that the viewer on the connection be given state, after the viewer has acted on the page. The server answers later with viewer_began or state_refused, and refuses it for a connection that already has a viewer (has_viewer) or whose viewer has not acted recently (no_gesture).
end_stateviewerEnds that viewer's state: every connection presenting it is told so, and the program hears viewer_left for each. A handle the channel does not hold is refused unknown_viewer.
offer_rememberconnectionAsks the browser to offer the viewer "remember me" on this channel; answered by state_refused when the connection has no viewer, is remembered already, or is private.
author_logconnections, level, E, W or I; text, 1 to 200 bytes; page or nullA line for the developer console of the viewer's receiver
loglevel, error, warn, info or debug; event, lower case, digits and _, at most 64 characters; text, at most 1,000 charactersA line for the server's log
packetsconnections, packets: base64 of whole 42-byte packetsRaw packets, delivered as they are. Each MUST be of a kind the stream may carry, or the line is refused with invalid_packet.
descriptionpage, the page describe named, and public. With public true, also title, 1 to 120 characters, text, 1 to 16,000 characters on one line, content, one sub-page of that page, and optionally picture, a ReGIS or NAPLPS picture shown in place of content's. With public false, nothing else.The answer to describe, and the only way a page becomes public on the web: see describing a page. A content of another page is refused with wrong_page, and one no describe awaits with not_awaited.
snapshot_pagesnapshot, the number the server's snapshot gave; page, one sub-page of the page asked for, of its sub-code, or of any sub-code when 3F7F was asked; picture, optional: {"kept": sub}, or a ReGIS or NAPLPS picture's data or parts, with a NAPLPS picture's objects, at most 262,144 bytes decodedThe answer to snapshot: the page as a stranger sees it, checked as every page and picture message is: see snapshots, for a program. One the server does not await, answered already or late, is refused not_awaited; one of another page or sub-code wrong_page; one naming a picture not kept not_kept.
snapshot_declinedsnapshotThe program will not draw this snapshot: the page is not drawn for strangers. One the server does not await is refused not_awaited. See snapshots, for a program.
measurerequest, a number from 0 to 232 less one that the program chooses; page, one sub-pageAsks what the sub-page's encoding costs. The server encodes it as for sending, sends it to no viewer, and answers measured or refused: see measuring a page.

A field that may be null may also be left out, and so may a redirect's unused fields. A refused answer carries the request of the message it refuses, when that message carried one. There is no cookie message: a program never chooses, sets or extends a viewer's handle, key or lifetime.

What reaches the viewer. Every packet is checked with the engine's one check of a stream. Sub-pages go as page frames, the index of reply and index as index records, subpages as SUBPAGES records, author_log as LOG records, redirect as a REDIRECT record, denied as a DENIED record, the Link Extension as LINKS records, sounds as audio records, a ReGIS or NAPLPS picture as its own records (REGIS and NAPLPS, DRAWING_LINKS, REGIS_CURSOR) to a receiver that agreed its language and as the mosaic fallback to any other, a rule table as RULES records, a state query as a RULES_QUERY record, the six commands as LOCAL_MIDI, VARIABLE, TIMER, REPORT, RUN and SEQUENCE records, an object_page as the object page's packets, frame as FRAME records, animate and a timeline's steps as ANIMATE records, sprites as a SPRITES record, naplps_objects as a NAPLPS_OBJECTS record, sprite_sheet as SHEET records, viewer state's requests as its own messages on the push connection, a snapshot_page as the page and picture records sent on the snapshot connections that asked for it, and packets as they are. Nothing of measure, measure_picture_text or snapshot_declined reaches a viewer.

Magazines. magazines is at most 8 objects, in ascending magazine, 1 to 8, each with a name of at most 120 characters and pages: 1 to 253, 251 in magazine 1, ascending, each page in that magazine and never reserved, with a title and a section of at most 120 characters, section null for none, and subpages, its count, 1 to 8,190. The index is page-level: sub-pages are never listed in it.

Rests on: EN 300 706 V1.2.1 clause 7.1.2 Packet address; EN 300 706 V1.2.1 clause A.10 Reserved page number; EN 300 706 V1.2.1 clause 9.6.1 Packets X/27/0 to X/27/3 for Editorial Linking

12.9 A sub-page

DOC-1971 · reference · normative · NeoTeletext's own: no standard defines it · requirements REQ-1064, REQ-1346, REQ-1478, REQ-1501, REQ-2214

Unfinished. The project's records do not show all of this as met, so it may not hold in full: REQ-1346 Server refuses a cursor outside DOC-1954 and still acknowledges input (to be rechecked on main); REQ-1478 A program sends one sub-page at a time as the engine's typed page model, field by field and bounded by the standard, never as TTI text (to be rechecked on livedevelopment); REQ-1501 Every page frame on a live connection carries exactly one sub-page (to be rechecked on main); REQ-2214 Protocol version 10 pages MUST carry the protocol 10 fields, and the server MUST encode their text (to be rechecked on livedevelopment).

A sub-page is the object a page, a reply, a measure and a description carry. Every field is required but cursor, character_set, language, level and text.

FieldHolds
page, subIts page, never a reserved number, and its sub-code, 0000 to 3F7E
rows25 entries, rows 0 to 24, each exact base64 of 40 seven-bit character codes, or null for a blank row. Row 0's columns 8 to 39 are the program's header text, and columns 0 to 7 are the receiver's.
linksThe six X/27/0 links: red, green, yellow, cyan, the fifth and the index, each page and sub, or null
display_row_24X/27/0's flag
link_extensionkeys: each key, red, green, yellow, cyan or index, at most once, with a target and a label of at most 9 characters, 8 for another service, null for the Index key. numbers: at most 8, a number on the page and a target, never web:. texts: at most 8, row 1 to 23, column 0 to 39, length keeping the run within 40 columns, and a target. A target is as the Link Extension says.
controlC4 to C11 as erase, newsflash, subtitle, suppress_header, update, interrupted_sequence, inhibit_display and magazine_serial. The server sets C4 and C11 itself.
character_setThe default character set: region, 0 to 15, carried in X/28/0 Format 1, or null for no X/28/0; and national_option, 0 to 7, carried in C12 to C14. Absent or null means region null and national option 0. It is never given with language, which sets the designation itself: a sub-page with both is refused with language_and_character_set.
languageThe page's default language, a tag of start.languages, or absent: see text in any language
levelneoteletext, the default when absent, or 3.5: the presentation level the page's text is written for
textAt most 64 runs of Unicode text, each with a row, a column, a text, an optional language and an optional outside, which the server writes over rows: see text in any language
enhancementsAt most 16 packets X/26, each designation 0 to 15 once, and 13 triplets of address, 6 bits, mode, 5 bits, and data, 7 bits
packetsAt most 16 other packed lines by packet: x27_nibbles, designation 1 to 3, with 39 nibbles of 4 bits; x27, designation 4 to 15; x28 and m29, designation 0 to 15, each of 13 triplets
cursorrow, column and block, or null

Examples of the forms: "links":[{"page":"101","sub":"3F7F"},null,null,null,null,null]; "link_extension":{"keys":[{"key":"red","target":"101","label":"NEXT"}],"numbers":[{"number":"101","target":"name:100"}],"texts":[{"row":1,"column":0,"length":4,"target":"101"}]}; "enhancements":[{"designation":0,"triplets":[{"address":41,"mode":0,"data":4}]}], with 13 triplets in all; "language":"el","text":[{"row":2,"column":1,"text":"Καλημέρα"}]; and an entry of packets names its form in a field packet, such as {"packet":"x27_nibbles",...}.

The server encodes the sub-page with the engine's encoder and sends it alone. A sub-page's links go with it every time it is sent.

A cursor is on rows 1 to 23 and columns 0 to 39, as the cursor record holds no other: row 0 is the header and row 24 the Fastext row. Any other is refused with the rule out_of_range, so the whole line is refused, and input to the page is still acknowledged with a cursor record of no cursor.

Rests on: EN 300 706 V1.2.1 clause 9.3.1 Page header; EN 300 706 V1.2.1 clause 9.3.1.2 Page sub-code; EN 300 706 V1.2.1 clause 9.3.1.3 Control bits; EN 300 706 V1.2.1 clause 9.3.1.4 Data bytes; EN 300 706 V1.2.1 clause 9.6.1 Packets X/27/0 to X/27/3 for Editorial Linking; EN 300 706 V1.2.1 clause 12.3 Non-spacing attributes and additional characters; EN 300 706 V1.2.1 clause 15 Character sets and their designation (the default character set the region and national option name); EN 300 706 V1.2.1 table 32 Function of Default G0 and G2 Character Set Designation and National Option (the region and national option of character_set); EN 300 706 V1.2.1 clause 9.4.2 Packet X/28/0 Format 1 (packet X/28/0 Format 1, which carries the region); EN 300 706 V1.2.1 table 4 Coding of packet X/28/0 Format 1 for basic Level 1 pages

12.10 Text in any language

DOC-2272 · reference · normative · NeoTeletext's own: no standard defines it · requirements REQ-2214

Unfinished. The project's records do not show all of this as met, so it may not hold in full: REQ-2214 Protocol version 10 pages MUST carry the protocol 10 fields, and the server MUST encode their text (to be rechecked on livedevelopment).

A program writes the words of a page as Unicode, each run of text naming its language, and the server encodes them into the page with the engine's one encoder. A program never encodes text itself, and never writes an ESC, a set switch or a character triplet for text.

The fields of a sub-page. Three fields of a sub-page carry text and its languages.

FieldHolds
languageThe page's default language, a tag of start.languages (from the server to a program), or absent. It sets the page's default G0 and G2 designation, which the server writes into the header's C12 to C14 and into packet X/28/0 Format 1, and it is the language of every run that names none. It is never given with character_set: a page with both is refused with language_and_character_set. An unknown tag is refused with unknown_language.
levelThe presentation level the text is written for: neoteletext, NeoTeletext's own receivers, the default when absent; or 3.5, Level 3.5 as EN 300 706 defines it.
textAt most 64 runs. Each has a row, 1 to 24; a column, 0 to 39; a text of 1 to 40 characters, in Unicode normalisation form C, with no control or bidirectional formatting character; a language, a tag of start.languages, or absent for the page's language, which is Latin English when the page names none; and outside, true when the run's text came from outside the program, such as what a viewer typed or a feed's data, and false when absent.

Cells. A run takes one cell for each character it shows, from its column rightwards, after combining marks have joined their letters, right-to-left text has been put in visual order, and Arabic letters have taken their joined forms. A run MUST end by column 39, or it is refused with text_out_of_columns, and MUST take no cell another run takes, or it is refused with text_overlap. Every cell no run takes keeps the program's own character code from rows.

How a run is written. No ESC is ever written. A run in the page's own set is written in the row's character codes, with its marked letters and G2 characters as X/26 triplets. A run in another set is reached, at the neoteletext level, by NeoTeletext's row set triplet (column mode 01010) at its first cell, and at the 3.5 level by a Modified G0 and G2 Character Set Designation triplet (column mode 01000) and a character triplet for each character, written over a space. A switch back to the page's own set follows at the cell after the run when the row shows anything after it.

The budget. The runs' triplets are merged with the program's own enhancements in the order EN 300 706 Annex A.4 gives, by row and then by column, and the whole MUST fit the 208 triplets of sixteen packets X/26, the Termination Marker included. A page that does not fit is refused with triplets_over_budget, naming the first run that does not fit.

What else is refused. A character the run's language cannot show, in a run not marked outside (text_unshown), so a channel's own text is caught by its tests. In a run marked outside such a character becomes the language's stand-in, the first of the question mark, the Arabic script's own question mark, a hyphen or a full stop that the language shows, the page is sent, and each character replaced is written once for each page message to the server's log as the event stand_in, naming the page, the code point, the stand-in and the language. outside came in protocol 10. A run on a cell where the program's own triplets place a character (text_cell_taken). A run whose row the program's own ESC codes or set triplets switch before it or within it (text_set_changed). Text on a page whose enhancements define objects (text_and_objects). A refusal names the run as page.text[n], or the field at fault within it.

The program's own X/28/0. With language, a program's own X/28/0 Format 1 in packets keeps every field but the designation, which the server writes.

The same page always encodes to the same bytes. A program can learn what its text costs before any viewer sees it by asking the server to measure the page.

Rests on: EN 300 706 V1.2.1 clause 15 Character sets and their designation (the character sets and their designation); EN 300 706 V1.2.1 table 32 Function of Default G0 and G2 Character Set Designation and National Option (the default G0 and G2 designation the page's language sets); EN 300 706 V1.2.1 table 33 Function of Second Language Designation and National Option Selection bits in packets (the second G0 designation); EN 300 706 V1.2.1 clause 9.4.2 Packet X/28/0 Format 1 (packet X/28/0 Format 1, which carries the designation); EN 300 706 V1.2.1 table 4 Coding of packet X/28/0 Format 1 for basic Level 1 pages (the coding of X/28/0 Format 1); EN 300 706 V1.2.1 clause 9.4.1 Packet X/26 (packet X/26, which carries the text's triplets); EN 300 706 V1.2.1 table 29 Function of Column Address triplets (column mode 01000, Modified G0 and G2 Character Set Designation, and the character triplets); EN 300 706 V1.2.1 clause A.3 Backwards compatibility in X/26 addressing (backwards compatibility in X/26 addressing); EN 300 706 V1.2.1 clause A.4 Addressing order for enhancement triplets (the order in which the triplets are merged)

12.11 Measuring a page

DOC-2276 · reference · normative · NeoTeletext's own: no standard defines it · requirements REQ-2216

Unfinished. The project's records do not show all of this as met, so it may not hold in full: REQ-2216 When a program sends measure, the server answers without sending the page to any viewer (to be rechecked on livedevelopment).

Because the server encodes a page's text (text in any language), a program cannot count what its text costs by itself. It asks the server, before any viewer sees the page.

typeFieldsWhat it does
measure, from the programrequest, a whole number from 0 to 232 less one that the program chooses for its own measurement, and not a selection's number; page, one sub-page exactly as a page message carries oneThe server encodes the sub-page as it would for sending, sends it to no viewer, and answers with measured, or with refused carrying the same request.
measured, from the serverrequest, the number given; triplets, the X/26 triplets the page uses, the program's own and its text's together, the Termination Marker included; limit, 208; designation, the page's default G0 and G2 designation as a value of EN 300 706 Table 32, and its second G0 designation as a value of Table 33 or null; runs, one entry for each text run in order, with the cells it takes on its row and the triplets it costThe answer. Nothing was sent to a viewer.

Every refusal names its request. A refused carries the request of the message refused when that message carried one, so a program that has sent several messages can tell which was refused. A refusal of text names the run as page.text[n], or the field at fault within it.

In a channel's tests. The TypeScript kit offers measure as a call that resolves to the measured answer or rejects with the refusal, so that a channel's own tests can measure every page they build against a running server, and a page that does not fit fails before it is deployed.

Rests on: EN 300 706 V1.2.1 table 32 Function of Default G0 and G2 Character Set Designation and National Option (the value measured gives as the default designation); EN 300 706 V1.2.1 table 33 Function of Second Language Designation and National Option Selection bits in packets (the value measured gives as the second G0 designation); EN 300 706 V1.2.1 clause 9.4.1 Packet X/26 (the packets X/26 whose triplets are counted)

12.12 Sounds

DOC-1972 · reference · normative · NeoTeletext's own: no standard defines it · requirements REQ-1060, REQ-1061, REQ-1062, REQ-1476

Unfinished. The project's records do not show all of this as met, so it may not hold in full: REQ-1060 Opus sound refused unless every packet is decodable by the receivers (to be rechecked on livedevelopment); REQ-1061 Opus carried unchanged as codec 2 (to be rechecked on livedevelopment); REQ-1062 PCM as IMA ADPCM, for microcontrollers (to be rechecked on livedevelopment); REQ-1476 The server and a program MUST exchange only the closed set of exactly typed messages, with no view field (to be rechecked on livedevelopment).

A sound message has a kind, and each has connections. The server turns it into the audio profile's records.

kindFields
opushandle 0 to 255, generation, packet_bytes 1 to 40, samples, packets: base64 of the packets back to back, at most two minutes. Every packet is checked with the engine's decoder against the profile.
opus_livehandle, generation, packet_bytes
opus_packetshandle, generation, packet_bytes, first, packets
objecthandle, generation, rate, 8000, 11025, 16000, 22050, 24000, 32000, 44100 or 48000, pcm: base64 of 16-bit little-endian mono samples, at most two minutes, encoded by the server as IMA ADPCM
livehandle, generation, rate
blockshandle, generation, rate, first, pcm
playchannel 0 to 3, handle, generation, gain 0 to 100, fade_ms, loop, after, duck 0 to 6, page or null
stopchannel, fade_ms
gainchannel, gain, fade_ms

12.13 Deadlines

DOC-1973 · reference · normative · NeoTeletext's own: no standard defines it · requirements REQ-1471, REQ-1481, REQ-6704

Unfinished. The project's records do not show all of this as met, so it may not hold in full: REQ-1471 The server holds a viewer's connection event for the first SELECT and sends the program one connected event (to be rechecked on livedevelopment); REQ-1481 A selection the program does not answer in time ends with DENIED 503 and the connection stays open (to be rechecked on livedevelopment); REQ-6704 The server keeps no session and sets no cookie: a connection lasts until it closes, and the program is told gone for it (not implemented on livedevelopment).

NameTimeWhat it bounds
PROGRAM_REPLY_LIMIT_MS, budgets.reply_limit_ms5,000 msHow long the server waits for an answer to connected or selected before it sends the viewer DENIED 503. It is provisional, and not yet measured.
FIRST_SELECTION_WAIT_MS1,500 msHow long connected is held for a connection's first SELECT
A closed connectionAt onceA connection that closes is told left and then gone at once: nothing waits for its viewer to come back, since the server keeps no session and offers no resumption
stats10 secondsHow often the figures are sent
Restarts1 to 30 secondsThe pause before a failing program is started again
ACKNOWLEDGEMENT_WAIT_MS250 msHow long an input count waits for a page frame to carry it before its cursor record goes alone. It is provisional, and not measured.
description_limit_ms2,000 msHow long a web visitor waits for a program's description. A later answer stands for those who come after, once.

A selection not yet answered keeps its deadline when its program ends, so its viewer is told the channel is unavailable. A program that started again is told of each connection by connected. A program that has no page yet answers reply with selectednull, and a page, redirect or denied after it.

12.14 What the kits give a program

DOC-1974 · concept · informative · NeoTeletext's own: no standard defines it · requirements REQ-1471, REQ-1674

Unfinished. The project's records do not show all of this as met, so it may not hold in full: REQ-1471 The server holds a viewer's connection event for the first SELECT and sends the program one connected event (to be rechecked on livedevelopment); REQ-1674 When a viewer opens a page of a live channel at an address with a query, the receiver MUST send the query in SELECT (to be rechecked on livedevelopment).

The TypeScript kit, neoteletext-server-ts-protocol (release 19.0.0), and the Python kit, neoteletext_app, wrap this protocol at version 16, and copy the request number, so that a program built on them never handles it. A kit keeps a screen for each page, and sends the rows as a whole sub-page when it is told to refresh. It sends a page's words as Unicode runs with their languages, for the server to encode (text in any language), and offers measure as a call that resolves to the measured answer or rejects with the refusal (measuring a page). It sends a page's rule table as the program builds it, and gives the program an input only when a rule of that table reported it, naming the rule. How the kits are built and released is in the part on the kits.

A kit gives each selection to a page's application as a request object, in the shape a web framework gives a request, before the page opens. It is called for every selection, so that its path is never stale, and with nothing once a selection without a query has left it behind.

KeyHolds
method"GET": a selection only ever reads a page, and a viewer's keys are not requests
pathThe place selected, as an address names it: 302 or 302/0002
queryThe query, by name. Of a name given twice, the last.
queryTextThe query as written, without its ?, undecoded

All of it but method is untrusted, from the viewer. There is no cookie in it: who the viewer is, when the viewer has given state, is the connection's viewer handle (viewer(connection)). On a page that keeps a copy for each connection, the UI library makes the page from the address's query, as it does from a redirect's params: ?article=5 reaches root(params).

12.15 Describing a page to the web

DOC-1975 · reference · informative · NeoTeletext's own: no standard defines it · requirements REQ-1728, REQ-6768

Unfinished. The project's records do not show all of this as met, so it may not hold in full: REQ-1728 A page is public on the web only when its channel's program says so (to be rechecked on main).

A page is public on the web only when its channel's program says so, page by page, and by default it is not. The server asks, and the program's answer is the only way a page becomes public. The answer goes to everyone, so a program builds it from no viewer.

typeFieldsWhat it does
describepage, and nothing else: no connection, session, cookie or queryFrom the server, when a web visitor or a search engine is at a page's address. A reserved page is not asked about.
descriptionpage, the page describe named, and public. With public true, also title, 1 to 120 characters, text, 1 to 16,000 characters on one line, content, one sub-page of that page, and optionally picture. With public false, nothing else.From the program, the answer. A content of another page is refused with wrong_page.

Not public. A page the program says is not public, a page that does not exist, a reserved page, and a page the program did not answer for within description_limit_ms, 2,000 ms, all give one answer: 200, the small page and noindex. It differs only in the address its link repeats, so an address says nothing of whether a private page exists.

Public. The page's title; a picture of the page, which the server draws from content and carries inline as a PNG data: address, left out over 64 KiB; the offer to open it or get NeoTeletext; a canonical link to <channel>NNN; and the text in <div class="paywall">, which the page's stylesheet hides.
